I then proceeded to the sales floor and located the multi-deck refrigeration system. The case temperature was elevated, with the case temperature at 42°F. I began troubleshooting System #7 and found that the unit was locked out on a high-discharge-pressure safety trip. I checked the discharge pressure and found it operating at approximately 330 PSI. I then verified the discharge pressure safety control and found it set to cut out at 400 PSI. Next, I inspected the condenser coil and found no visible obstructions; however, the condenser fins were damaged in several areas. I also checked the liquid line filter drier for any signs of restriction and found none. After power-cycling the controller to restart the system, the unit tripped again on high discharge pressure. I then performed a thorough cleaning of the condenser coil until the rinse water ran clear. Once cleaning was completed, I restarted the system and monitored operation. After cleaning, the system operated normally and did not trip on high discharge pressure.

Then, I installed service ports on the liquid line dryers and the suction fill-up spot on the compressor for both circuits. The blast chiller operates on two circuits. I took the unit out of a defrost the temps went up to about 17 degrees then started dropping again
Unit is now working and there are no more alarms present
If there is another issue I recommend changing out the filter drier

E7BBF418-6B8A-4636-BE72-2E8CBE32A27D.root_cause: Found a fuse blown. Had to source new fuse as it is not a common style fuse (age of unit). Got the blower motor up and running. Called Tunilabs back to put unit into test, found that the controller would run it in Free-cool, but not turn compressor on. Went through all electrical transformers, and contactor coils to ensure no other issues. Ran continuity test through both safeties and oil control up to the contactor, safeties are good to go. With the temps in the low to mid 30°s there is something holding out control voltage, either a freeze stat on the evap coil, one of the multiple controllers due to ambient temp. Also getting the unit properly charged in these temps would not work. Will need to do more testing when the weather is warmer, spring PM. Traced the issue back to 2 blown 15amp fuses that energize the transformer that powers up the control circuit. Once new fuses were installed, got comms back up. Called Tunilabs again and had the unit forced into cool, still got no control voltage. Again traced the wiring back to the Bellimo module that would not power up. This module sends control voltage through the correct pathways for either cool/heat. Found that there was no power getting through the control circuit at all. Nothing to the compressor module, nothing to through the safeties, no voltage out of electrical box at all other than primary voltage. Will need to return with another tech to sort out the wiring as it is been modified/re wired over the years and no wire numbers put on the modified wiring. Likely culprit is the Bellimo module, the RTCR board or the relay board. Will have to remove the larger panels to properly check the wiring. Whatever took out those fuses likely shorted something else in the control circuit. Started with tracing out voltage drop to Belimo controller, traced it back to a fuse holder connector. Then began tracing control voltage to compressor 1 contactor. This brought us to the old style relay board, found missing relays, bad relays and some creative wiring already in place. After a few wiring adjustments we were able to get the compressor contactor active when called for cooling. Next we wired in the hi/low safeties, oil pressure safety. This piece of equipment needs 3 things to make it work. 1) water in the de-superheater/ Evap-a/way pan. 2) factory rated air flow across condensing unit. It is undersized and even a small amount of dirt causes the compressor to overheat. 3) Enriched sub cooler at evaporator. I had to cool the compressor’s discharge gas temperature by adding ice to the de-superheater pan. I had to clean the honeycombs and condenser coil again, just like last time. And I had to set superheat on the TXV at the outlet of the sub cooler. Liquid refrigerant was so hot by the time it hit the sub cooler that it did nothing to cool the liquid and nothing to cool the compressor. Over enriched the TXV to compensate for high operating temperatures. Set superheat at outlet of the sub cooler. Dropped operating pressure by 30#s by balancing case operation. *This case needs monthly PM service to keep it running. It’s location next to the front door and service counter make it a high traffic area that requires more attention. Poor housekeeping. The unit is parked next to the front door which affects liquid line temp and discharge temps. Poor placement of the unit is the cause of all of this.

Compressor 3 still tripping on oil failure and not feeding oil. Found both the oil pickup screen and inlet screen plugged up. Cleaned both screens and compressor is feeding oil properly. It is likely that all the oil screens on Rack A are very dirty. Oil coming out of the compressor is black. Recommend full rack oil change, as well as changing oil filter and filter driers. On arrival found only comp 1 running on rack a. 3,4,5 off on oil fail. Frosting on oil differential valve. Pumped down and pulled apart debris in valve metering oil. Also checked inlet screens for comp 3,4,5. 3 clean from previous cleaning. 4,5 were dirty cleaned and reassembled took vaccine and got rack back online. While pulling down differential valve clogged again. Pulled apart cleaned. Watched all systems come to temp. Even though we are waiting on compressor we should do full oil change/ oil differential sooner as there may be more debris inside top half of valve we cannot clean.

8309EC6C-52AF-4CA8-AC68-BE6D08969CB1.root_cause: Verified the defrost circuit and found the line voltage defrost breaker had failed, preventing proper power from being supplied to the defrost circuit. Replaced the failed line voltage breaker and retested circuit operation. During operational checks, determined the defrost circuit was still not energizing correctly. Continued troubleshooting and traced the fault to a failed defrost contactor with defective contacts preventing voltage from passing through the circuit under load. A suitable replacement contactor was not available on-site and will need to be sourced before repairs can be completed. Once the correct contactor is obtained, it will need to be installed to restore proper defrost circuit operation. Returned to site following replacement of the failed line voltage defrost breaker and restoration of the defrost control circuit. Verified proper operation of the replacement breaker and confirmed the defrost contactor is energizing and switching correctly. Performed additional diagnostics on the evaporator defrost circuit and isolated the remaining fault to an open top coil heater. Confirmed the upper coil heater has failed electrically and will require replacement. The lower coil heater remains operational, allowing the case to continue completing defrost cycles and maintain acceptable operation.

When testing the compressor with load i get a very high current ( 120A) , compared to when it has not load ( 8A) The diagnostic is either bad winding ( for higher voltage) or a shortened motor. Confirmed the new compressor is bad.

Observed significant frost accumulation on the suction line consistent with evaporator floodback. Diagnosed failed suction line temperature sensor producing erroneous superheat calculations. Returned to troubleshoot Case A16B and identified an incorrectly sized SPW-2 valve cartridge contributing to excessive refrigerant feed, suction line frosting, and floodback conditions. 0A92CDBC-3D27-40E5-81C2-6520B1723A85.root_cause: Only issue I found was stage five compressor on rack A was off on run proof. Reset high-pressure control compressor turned on no other issues at this time.

72228274-5C77-4F97-8E0C-45CF673D52E5.root_cause: Found Blower motor overload (Schneider LRD-35) control contacts stuck open. Found VFD frequency on L2 load side imbalanced by +40% from L1 and L3. This is what damaged the integrity of the blower motor windings and eventually blew the fuse on L2. Found that existing VFD FLA are rated for 31 amps and blower motor is rated for 29.5 amps indicating that VFD is undersized for this drive motor. Recommending that a 30hp 40 FLA VFD is installed to ensure that drive does not operate at more then 70% of its FLA guarantee that drive will live long healthy life (approximately 30+ years). Found that control wiring for blower motor overload (LRD-35) was positioned in the control circuit after the time delay relay for the bypass contactor, causing the overload not to protect the motor in VFD operations, in turn allowing the VFD to damage the motor when the VFD failed. Re-wired overload to be in play and protect the blower motor from over amping whether it’s in VFD or Bypass operations.

The gaskets must be replaced so the doors close properly and ice does not accumulate; photos of the required parts are attached. Required parts: 5 gaskets, 1x 3090935KT (Innovator Door Bottom Socket Kit), 1x 3090933KT (Innovator Door Top Hinge Kit), 1x HATF9042AAG240 relay, 1x HAT903CSAC 220 relay.

I then achieved a 6°F superheat and the left case successfully pulled down to temperature and began cycling normally. I disassembled the right case as necessary and replaced the faulty case temperature sensor. After installation, I verified the new sensor in an ice bath and confirmed it was reading 32°F. After allowing the case to run, the right case began cycling normally and maintaining proper temperature. We will return. Returned to site. Spoke with Dennis and Josh and we all agreed to replace the TXV on the left deli case. I pumped down the circuit. I unbraized the filter drier and the old txv. Braized in a new filter drier and new txv body. Installed a cartridge and power head on the txv. Placed circuit in a vacuum. After vacuum I opened system and let cases drop down in temp. Took a while to dial in superheat on new tvx. This case is now showing 37 degrees and cycling on and off. The case on the right I had to play with and keep adjusting the txv as well. 6C8EAE8F-9E40-476D-9433-3025977F7403.root_cause: Found that the case temperature would not pull below 45°F. Verified evaporator fan motor operation and confirmed the fan was rotating in the correct direction. Checked thermostat operation and verified it was properly cycling the compressor on and off. Connected gauges to the service ports at the condensing unit and found the system was low on refrigerant. Performed a leak search using an electronic leak detector and leak detection bubbles. Located a refrigerant leak at the suction service valve. When attempting to remove the service port cap, refrigerant immediately began leaking from the valve. Attempted to remove the top cap of the suction king valve to inspect the valve stem position and determine if it was partially seated, allowing refrigerant to escape. The cap was severely rusted and seized. Applied WD-40 and cleaned the area with sandpaper in an attempt to free the cap; however, it would not loosen. Excessive force could not be applied without risking damage to the suction line. Will need to order and replace the leaking suction king valve. Once the replacement valve is on site, return visit will be required to recover refrigerant as needed, replace the valve, pressure test the system with nitrogen, perform a complete leak check, evacuate the system, and recharge with refrigerant. Cleaned up work area and documented findings with pictures and notes. System is currently operating at approximately 50% capacity. Return visit required once parts are received. Compressor energized but was not pumping refrigerant. Verified voltage and found the overload protector tripping due to excessive compressor temperature. Allowed the compressor to cool using a bag of ice and attempted to restart after it had completely cooled, but the compressor still would not pump. Verified all electrical components were operating properly, confirming a failed compressor, most likely caused by operating without refrigerant. Disconnected power to the unit to prevent store personnel from plugging it back in and causing additional damage. Unit is 100% down. Recommend do not plug in or attempt to operate until compressor is replaced. Office to order replacement compressor.

41626F10-B6A0-4456-8379-FCE982DE6AD4.root_cause: Inspection revealed frost accumulation around the TXV and liquid line components. Superheat readings were elevated and unstable, indicating the evaporator was being starved of refrigerant. Further evaluation identified a temperature drop across the liquid line filter drier consistent with a restriction. The restricted filter drier is limiting liquid refrigerant flow to the TXV, resulting in reduced evaporator feed and poor case pull-down performance. TXV operation was evaluated by making adjustments and monitoring system response. Although temporary changes in suction pressure and superheat were observed, the valve failed to maintain consistent refrigerant control and continued to underfeed the evaporator. Findings indicate a restricted liquid line filter drier and a failed TXV requiring replacement. Further troubleshooting found a restricted liquid line ball valve on circuit 2.2. Pumped the circuit down, replaced the valve, and restored liquid flow. Solid liquid was confirmed at the evaporator, but the TXV failed to modulate properly, indicating an internal failure.

Under further investigation, I determined there had been a planned power outage. The compressors remained energized while the condenser fan motors lost power, causing excessive head pressure to build until the relief valve opened. Once power was fully restored, I brought the rack back online and verified proper operation. I then added 75 lbs of R-407A refrigerant to restore the receiver level to 20%. After charging the system, I monitored operation and verified that all cases reached and maintained proper setpoint temperatures. I also verified that the rack was maintaining proper suction pressure. I ended up brazing it unconventional style since the elbows are paper thin. Pulled deep vacuum on that half of condenser. Performed decay negative pressure test. Performed positive pressure test. Put back into circulation. Added 25 lbs of refrigerant. Added one gallon of oil. All of rack b is back up and functioning. Verified all temps came down to set point.

So at that moment, I thought bad transducer then close my valve and remove the transducer and went to my van to get another transducer. I installed the new transducer and opened my valve back up. I then checked my pressure and my pressure was still reading the same as the original transducer. So I did cut the wire connecting the transducer to the controller and made a new wire connection. After making the new wire connection, of the controller still read the same pressure as before. So I started to read the manual, learn how to use the controller, and called RDM for assistance on the programming for the controller. Unfortunately, RDM tech-support could not login to the 594 H-E-B location. Through the process of RDM tech support walking through the procedure, the case controller program was removed from 3 out of 4 controllers on the meat case. So I continue to look into my controller and figure out what P5 meant and why am I transducer was reading a different pressure for my gauges. I compared the controller from the case I was working on to the case that was in operational condition. After going through the parameters and comparing the two case controllers, I came to the conclusion that the case I was working on had the complete wrong parameters. So I went through each parameter and took notes on the difference between the two cases. I’ve been started to reprogram this case through the case controller.

E31632ED-ECB1-40B4-A76B-01E1C6DE0ABD.root_cause: Found no water flow from supply. Inspected Belimo actuator and found valve spring-returned closed due to power interruption. Suspect improper valve operation caused weak water supply and incomplete saturation of fill media, reducing adiabatic efficiency and contributing to repeated high gas cooler/max pressure alarms, potential relief events, and low liquid alarms. Verified control signal and confirmed 2 VDC is command to fully open and 10 VDC to fully closed in this application. Tested actuator by removing power and found valve failing open, which does not match system logic. Suspect actuator was indexed incorrectly and operating in reverse. Adjusted actuator by reversing polarity to fail-closed configuration to match 2–10 VDC control logic. Confirmed signal and feedback not matching and confirmed strong water flow with full saturation of media pads during demand.

8E7325F6-2287-4F2C-9A10-4D19F16C398A.root_cause: Dairy walk in cooler REDA11 has 2/4 evaporators that have bad EEV coils. Magnets placed on valves by previous tech.  Coils not available locally . This method, used as an emergency temporary fix, works in many instances. In this rare case it flooded compressors and  they tripped on discharge pressure. Without EEV coils available the two evaporators will not hold proper temperature, they will maintain in the high 40’s, 48-49 degrees; too warm . Magnets are needed to force EEV’s open. A solution is to install liquid line ball valves at each evaporator that has bad EEV coils , Evaporators REDA11c and 11d. Ball valves can be closed a certain percentage to regulate flow of refrigerant. Pumped down entire dairy circuit. Installed ball valves. Vacuum pulled. Opened up refrigeration. Leak searched. No leaks . After adjusting ball valves in small increments determined that they needed to be opened only 1/8 of a turn . Anything greater would cause liquid refrigerant to flood compressors at Rack. After monitoring rack and line temperatures all 4 evaporators at 36-37 degrees.

Comp 3, 2/3 full. Comp 4, full. The ball in the bottom sight glass on the reservoir was bouncing. It’s believed there was floodback that never got resolved. Overtime, oil kept being pumped in and the oil pots opened to have the oil overcome the floodback. The Y valve was set high again to force oil into the oil pots. Checked out oil issues. The motor did not turn on at all. I had power but not going through to the motor for some reason. I began tracing wire back and found a toggle switch and opened up the switch plate and began testing power and it wasn't going through the toggle switch to the thermostat. I then bypassed the toggle switch and the fan still didn't come on. I then went to another rack and found that the thermostat was set to 90 degrees, I returned and it was set to 100 degrees. I put the thermostat to 90 degrees and the fan turned on. The motor turned on for about 10 seconds and shut off. I was wondering why it was cycling on and off every 30 seconds and then on for 10 seconds then back off. I then searched online for the diagram and found it. It was set to 115 volts while the motor needed to be set to 230 volts. Cut power again and moved connections to turned the universal motor to 230 volts and the motor began running great but running in reverse. I then searched and read some more on how to switch the fan from clockwise to counter clockwise. Moved connections around one more time and got the fan to operate properly.

Or see if there is some other underlying issue to the continued freeze up of this line up. Specs state this style case with electronic defrost in the return should do one defrost a day with a 60 min fail safe a defrost termination of 49° and a 15 min drip time. Set up was currently 3 defrosts a day with a 5 min drip time and 30 min fail safe. There is no defrost termination setup in the controller. I did push the units into a defrost and allowed them to run a full hour and none of them exceeded the 49° termination temp and they all went full defrost. I changed the defrost schedule from the original to two defrosts a day at 60 min per defrost and a 15 min drip time. As per hill phoenix spec sheets and tech support. This should remedy the continued freeze ups on this line up.

4B8B825B-2220-4AF9-87F0-111D729B94ED.root_cause: Found LPRV valve fully opened, outdoor temperatures were in the high 50’s with caused low discharge pressures; set valve to auto and monitored ops, receiver level immediately dropped to normal range 18-25%, adjusted LPRV to 90 PSI out of sub-cooler with all fans on. LPRV being restricted allows head pressure to build which causes fans to turn on at cut in set point and off once it reaches low set point. If LPRV remains open, fans will remain energized due to never reaching fans cut out/ low set point thus causing liquid refrigerant to puddle on receiver from low liquid pressure.

A87BD562-9762-4DE8-80A3-82D94879502B.root_cause: I noticed the drain pans and piping were sweating so I took temperatures of the room and condensate pipes. I found they were all reading 32 degrees. I used my CO2 drain gun to blow out the pipes and verify they did not have any blockages further down. These units will periodically go into a defrost cycle to melt ice off the coil, txv, and piping. This allows the condensate to go down the drain, but as it runs down the cold piping, it can freeze up again. Over time that ice will build up and block the drain completely. That will cause the ice to keep building up in the pipe all the way back to the unit. This is what was happening to cause the dripping on Friday. The condensate pipes and unit filled up with ice and would melt/drip from the defrost cycle. Once I blew out the drain lines, I picked up all the insulation needed for units. Before putting it on, I took the room and pipe temperatures again and they read 35-36 degrees. I still ran my heat gun over the drain lines to ensure there was nothing frozen inside. Once I knew the pipes were clear, I wrapped them with the insulation. Found drain pans heavily iced up, drain line frozen as well due to cooler setpoint at 40 psi (404a) increased pressure to 60 psi also closed ball valve on one blower to allow ice to thaw will return tonight to de-ice drain pan and drain line no temperature issues prior to leaving location

I went to Tropic to get a new pressure switch, but when I went to replace it, I found that the king valve on the suction line, where the switch was supposed to be, didn't have threads and had a slight leak. I made sure there were no leaks using nitrogen. After that, I vacuumed the system for half an hour and charged the unit with 2.5 pounds of R407C, which is what the unit originally had. After all the ice was melted with hot water we were then able to get an accurate superheat reading on the case and able to adjust it properly and let it do its thing. We adjusted all cases down to case spec superheat which is 6-8 degrees. We also took out all the driers in the 4 separate circuits we worked on due to being clogged and causing severe temp drop across it. To do so we pumped down each circuit and then proceeded to cut out the driers and just replace it with a stick of 3/8. After each time I double checked my welds and then we would pull a vacuum down to below 500 microns before starting circuit back up. By doing all of this we were able to get the rack superheat down from 70 to 42, Helping this rack immensely. Verified refrigeration and defrost cycle. Identified 3 deck case. Asked for product to be pulled in order to access the entire evaporator coil and silicone the cracks where leaks are caused. Cut liquid line and suction line in order to get behind the evap coil to seal the case. Sealed old cracks with silicone. Cleaned case. Connected liquid line and suction line back together. Pulled a vacuum under 500 microns on the case. Turned refrigeration back on. Turned power back onto the case. Case pulled down to temp. Reached defrost termination temp. Let Butyl settle then brazed back copper line set with copper couplings making sure to flow nitrogen to reduce cubric oxide. Pulled deep vacuum below 200 microns and perform tightness test. 9139D920-0ADE-46B4-8BF0-7467AD0AD7B8.root_cause: This drain pan has been an issue since it’s been installed last year. There has been so much silicone added to this drain pan at this point it has to be replaced. Found pan iced up and drain was clear but due to the amount of silicone near the drain hole it creates a lip for the water to have to get over before draining. Once I got the whole thing Deiced I was able to see the water is leaking through the actual drain to the secondary pan and flooding out. There is a large gap between the two pans which creates a vacuum lock for the water and traps it not allowing it to get over the silicone until it finally freezes over. I was able to remove a lot of the silicone and apply a small layer of pan spray around the drain opening to seal it up from inside and also applied a bead of silicone on the exterior to seal up the gap. At this time, the leak has been subsided, but this pan has to be replaced before it starts leaking again. Unit was found with evap coil partially covered in ice. After removing ice buildup, we removed damaged drain pan and installed replacement pan. We then added new hardware to confirm seal. Pan has been replaced and is no longer leaking.

Began troubleshooting the space temp and found a loose wire on the I-Controller. Repaired the wire and space temp was now reading accurately. After going back and forth with tech support it was determined that Siemens was out here on the 19th and claims the wire from the RTU to the terminal block is bad. I Ohmed out the wire and was getting 8-9 ohms they want it under 7. Pulled up IMS manuals and it’s not wired to their gateway. Sent a support ticket to IMS to obtain further information on how it should be wired and to let them know that the E2 is no longer monitoring or controlling the RTU. Followed the instructions that IMS sent and tied the RTU into port 4 on the gateway. Once I landed it in the RTU the VCCX controller would go offline. After going through the wiring schematic found that the Bacnet and Modus wires were swapped on the terminal block. Landed the wires in the correct location on the terminal block. Then landed the Siemens and IMS cables in the correct location. The modbus and and bacnet came on. Got on the Siemens site link and the RTU is now displaying data.

08F412E8-D533-43F9-949A-0CC5CCFF77E8.root_cause: Inspected the gas cooler and noticed the adiabatic pads were plugged up. Also noticed the ball/relief valve for the gas cooler inlet coil on the right side was leaking at the relief valve. Checked the sump area of the gas cooler and it was dry but was full of sand. Removed the sand and tested the fill valve. There was no water entering the sump. Had to tap on the water fill valve to unclog it. Tested the sump pump and there was no water coming out of the feed lines and going down the adiabatic pads. Removed the adiabatic pads and tested the sump pump again. Upon removing the pads noticed the coils on both sides were damaged due to deterioration. There was still poor water flow on both sides with the pads removed. Used a thermostat screw driver to try and clear some of the plugged holes. Removed the caps of the water feed lines on both ends and the lines were plugged with calcium. Cleaned both water lines to remove the calcium then went through and cleared each hole. Tested the sump pump again and there is now adequate water flow. To prevent further damage to the coils used a water hose and rinsed the salt off of the coils and the pads. The store is 1.5 miles from the ocean. There has also been an extensive amount of construction around the store. Both of which are contributing to the deterioration and cleanliness of the gas cooler. The pads are too damaged and plugged to thoroughly clean. Tried to use city pressure water and they were falling apart. Tried to clean the coils using city pressure water and the fins were falling off. All adiabatic pads, both coils, and one discharge inlet ball/relief valve need to be replaced.

I began by bringing all supply's & materials needed & did a small vacuum to recovery tank before starting recovery machine on, recovered refrigerant in totaled i recovered 17lbs what factory charge was labeled for & shut off main voltage for both circuits to stop running removed condenser motor & began un welding txv as well as 3/8 filter drier, prep area for new txv for it sanded down as well as filter drier & began bracing new txv into place mounted sensing bulb on suction line & braced new filter drier with liquid line , added nitrogen to pressurize system with 150psi pressure hold for 15 minutes & released air from nitrogen then began Vaccum system into 500 microns & recharged system with factory charge 17lbs of 410a refrigerant. Turned the system on & monitored pressures & temperatures on unit, leak searched unit confirmed 0 leaks with soap bubbles & system was left running good. E5BEA142-4CED-4FD3-B512-CFBC00216C7C.root_cause: Found compressor locked out on oil control. Reset unit to clear code and run compressor found oil level low due to float failure in oil separator. Upon arrival I checked in with IVR and the manager on site. I also checked in with the engineers. Went up to the rooftop, and the unit was turned off. I flipped the power back on, and it did not come on for a little while, and then it finally came on after a short delay. However, I noticed inside of the side glass of the compressor. There was hardly any oil in there. While the unit was running, I could see that the oil level was getting less and less as it was running. I added oil into the compressor and watched it run for a little while and eventually all of the oil in the compressor was sucked out. I decided to look into why we’re not getting oil return into the compressor. After some troubleshooting, I found that the time delay for the oil return solenoid was bad. It was not opening up the oil return solenoid to return oil back to the compressor as needed. I replaced the oil return timer with a timer from my truck stock. I tested the new timer and it is working properly. The oil level is staying within a good range now. While observing and troubleshooting, I noticed that the shut off valve for the suction line at the service ports was broken and eventually will create a leak in the refrigeration. Well, submit a quote to replace the shut off valve. It is 1 inch piping. System is operating properly at this time. Need to submit quote

4A8B2925-B9A4-4780-9D69-B7DA4D3E16DF.root_cause: Self-contained unit with berries was making a loud noise due to the condenser fan motor. Replaced condenser fan motor.

61447C79-E2B6-4ADE-ABF7-F5C69C0068CB.root_cause: Found condenser B motor bad. Found no belt.

E94D4948-D958-4E26-AAC3-5C25C343DB7B.root_cause: Performed leak search and found coremax valve on discharge line leaking at over 8000 ppm.

C22E6E1B-F4E9-4F51-92DA-E489840051BD.root_cause: *UNDER CONSTRUCTION: Replace 3 evap coils and 2 condensing units*

931F28A9-C7B4-4C20-8610-2288313689DE.root_cause: Found leaks in the middle deli case on bottom coil at factory weld

9D75F532-B1D7-4FE2-8B22-F80F6698E84C.root_cause: Found defrost pan relay starting to show some wear. Replaced relay as preventative maintenance.

7D425B66-0B6C-450F-BE1B-D7AEDDC16D87.root_cause: Located small leak on discharge valve at Rack M2 compressor 5. RH side bolt was needed to be tightened. Leak is now gone. Added 25# of 407a, low liq alarm cleared.

E5EE42BA-ABB2-4E8F-BAC9-4684A577EA07.root_cause: Found 2 motors dead on 2b multi deck.

Leak checked Rack, leaks are repaired, none others found.

CE225159-B291-455A-8C18-8E5574B51995.root_cause: Found and replaced plugged TXV screen.

D23750C9-C64F-4707-B25D-F1EFFDBAFBB5.root_cause: I inspected the motor and it was close to being seized and I could hear the bearings going out.

7B2F603D-F74B-48A1-9141-3448A54921CF.root_cause: Leak checked and found very large leak in deli service case at liquid line heat exchanger

F788B586-65EB-47CF-BDF0-4A2FE1EC6315.root_cause: I found the left motor had shorted out and blew the fuses.

2DF6B3C3-DBE8-4A85-BBA0-02F91B587A2E.root_cause: Cases iced up due to faulty time clock.

Confirmed unit held its vacuum for some time without rising then slowly opened the ball valves allowing unit’s refrigerant to begin flowing. Checked super heat finding all units to be within range. Monitored the units drop in temperature and maintain at set point for some time. Found case C thermometer was reading about 10-15 degrees off of the RDM controller so then removed it and installed a new one. 3E9C418F-C335-429E-AA24-DDC3FFCF3EC3.root_cause: I checked in using the third-party app and then with the on-site MIC. I proceeded to rack G and found compressor #1 tripped on oil failure. Upon inspection, there was no oil in the oil float. I then checked the oil separator and found it also had no oil. I inspected the remaining compressors and found that compressor #3 was overfilled with oil. I isolated the issue by closing the oil inlet to compressor #3 and pumped out the excess oil until it reached the proper level. After correcting this, I verified that the oil receiver was full. I rechecked compressor #1 and confirmed it had proper oil levels. I located the oil receiver and found it empty. I then inspected all compressors and verified that each compressor maintained a proper oil level, with no indication of oil being trapped or not returning. I attempted to pump oil from the lower level back to the rack, but this did not resolve the issue after multiple attempts. I then checked oil pressure and inspected the oil separator; both were found to be operating correctly with no issues. I shut off the oil supply to each compressor, allowing the oil receiver to fill. The receiver filled as expected. I then reopened the oil supply to the compressors, and the receiver level dropped back to empty, indicating normal oil circulation throughout the system. The 2 TXVs need to be returned. I located the outside air temperature sensor and replaced it. I verified pressures, saturation temperatures, superheat, and sub cooling. RTU3 is cooling as intended. Call is complete.

I contacted the on-call manager and we worked through several troubleshooting steps, but the issue persisted. The on-call manager arrived on site with replacement boards and installed new boards for positions 3 and 5. After replacement, both boards came online successfully and communication to the E2 controller was restored. I monitored the system and verified proper operation with no additional issues found at this time. Billable - boards failed due to phase loss, pic attached.

Removed panel covering the eev and found eev is not pulsing. Removed bottom kick plate to access controller. Confirmed 120v at terminal block. Confirmed 120v at common on controller. Tested voltage at NC and found controller was not pulsating voltage to control the eev. Killed power and jumped power to eev. Restore power to test eev. This eev opened and began feeding. This shows this controller has gone bad and is no longer controlling relay 1. Sourced new 740 controller from climate pros inventory. Replaced old controller. Confirmed type, unit and ID before replacing. unit-19, type 4, id 158. Replaced controller. Confirmed each wiring placement. Installed controller and reprogrammed. Started controller up. While asset in recovery, rdm began a defrost. Terminated defrost manually and allowed asset to drop into temp. Asset dropped to 43 degrees and balances out. Accessed controller parameters and found parameters did not automatically download when setting ID. Accessed adjacent controller and noted all parameters. Returned to 06a controller and plugged in all proper parameters. Asset not programmed properly. Cycled controller to confirm parameters have held. Called HEB EMS and spoke to LEE, went through parameters and operation with EMS. Confirmed controller is now running properly. Informed and checked out with MiC. Work is now complete asset at 28 degrees.

09508F1E-3C18-4893-A85D-246E360F7784.root_cause: During further inspection, I observed physical damage to the right-side panel, likely caused by a pallet jack. The sidewall has separated, allowing condensation to form inside the panel and drip down the case. I contacted the manufacturer for repair guidance, and they provided a full list of parts required to replace the damaged wall assembly. As a temporary measure, they recommended applying silicone to the affected area to help slow condensation buildup until permanent repairs can be completed. Upon arrival, I checked in through the third-party application and then checked in with the on-site MIC. I located the Healthy Living case and confirmed that both side panels required replacement. After removing all mounting screws, we carefully removed the old defective panel, which revealed the source of the water leakage. Once the panel was removed, I ensured the mounting surface was completely dry and removed all excess silicone from the previous installation to ensure a proper seal for the new panel. The trim from the old panel was removed and transferred to the new panel. I then applied Volkem sealant to the mating surfaces where the panel and case would seal together. Once the sealant was applied, I installed the new panel, secured all mounting screws, and verified that the panel was properly aligned and tightly fastened. After allowing the sealant to set, I repeated the same procedure on the opposite side panel. Once both panels were installed and secured, I reassembled the case components and verified that the drain lines were clear and unobstructed. While waiting for the sealant to fully cure, I installed the anti-sweat motor underneath the case. After completing the installation, I reassembled the entire case and restored it to operation. I monitored the unit and verified that it reached and maintained the proper setpoint temperature. I also confirmed that the condensate pump was operating correctly. At this time, both side panels have been successfully replaced, the anti-sweat motor has been installed, and the water leak onto the sales floor has been resolved. The unit is operating properly and cooling as designed.

Before wiring, I fabricated the rest of the suction line coming from the ball valve. Brazed all the lines in, including the new Roto-lock. Pulled vacuum on compressor and suction line. While vacuum was going I wired up the new OMB oil control and compressor itself. Vacuum was complete and I reintroduced the compressor to refrigerant. Changed the contactor and aux and proceeded to start the compressor. Found compressor spinning the correct direction and operating how it should be. Verified operations and checked out with Merrik Williamsen.

A 6 degree threshold is more commonly medium temp settings. Also found condensing temp to only be about 7 degrees above ambient causing rack to not be rejecting as much heat as it should. Which in turns causes our cases to struggle. Case a31.4 temp at 3.5 on departure. Which is lowest it’s been in a while. A more permanent fix would be for us to schedule with winco a call for us to balance out entire loop. Demerched the txv section of each case. Checking each case found temp drops between 4 and 8° across all filter driers. Had manager put in separate work order to replace rack filter cores as we have had multiple cases with filter driers clogged. Pumped down circuit. Recovered refrigerant back into rack. Removed and replaced all 4 filter driers on cases for a31. Pulled vacuum on circuit. Opened and allowed to drop temp. Had to then work on balancing cases. As they were not balanced well. Reset txvs stems to factory setting. Had to open further from factory due to tonnage of valves and btus of cases. Had issue balancing cases due to high load on cases from pull-down and cases not being at setpoint for a long time but full of product. Also had issue due to customers opening doors for extended periods constantly. Found leak on the liquid header Schrader. Closed down king valve and replaced core. Opened king valve and verified leak stopped. Continued and found no additional leaks. Charged rack A with 150lbs of 407A until the bottom receiver float reach the top of the sight glass. Liquid level is now at 15-25% and no longer alarming.

I then troubleshooted unit & upon further inspection i added 3& 1 compressor producer & compressor stayed running then I pierced unit with tool & found unit on 0psi & then I added nitrogen & then found leak at liquid line that factory had soldered copper line. True tech support went ahead & told me they will ship out a new compressor with capillary tube new filter drier & line set will arrive at shop from 2-3 business days.

8135CC29-8C43-4AEE-9294-6216742D6BAE.root_cause: Found fan #1 very noisy and hitting against plenum and fan #2 dead. Likely due to iced up case from clogged drain. Replaced both fan motors.

BECA7119-80FA-4180-A4A5-A4701511E0B7.root_cause: Roof leak dripping onto electrical cabinet got into contactor shorting it out.

93171A9C-6E04-49A0-A687-4CDAC4EF7123.root_cause: Picked up 1048ppm at discharge header transducer, removed valve cap and found Schrader core hanging out and could feel pressure coming from valve. Tighten valve core and leak stopped. Leak repaired.

72ED01B8-EA79-47B9-9856-65F7CAB3EE2E.root_cause: Upon further inspection found top hinge assembly burnt. Excessive condensation around frame which likely caused hinge pin to arc. Checked anti-sweat operations on door, no voltage present. Checked all other doors on same case verified anti-sweat heaters working and receiving power. Removed door and inspected frame plug and hinge pin, both burnt need to be replaced.

7A38D239-65EA-4D87-85D3-E1440FFE84AB.root_cause: Found case running at 37° with poor airflow in middle of case. Took apart case and found a bad fan motor. Replaced motor.

2FB52C62-4BA0-4DAB-AEB1-69BC02AE14FE.root_cause: Noticed oil in reservoir was low, due to split solenoids on condenser leaking (written up 3-18).

4E5EA822-CF35-428B-A137-5DDFFD86A02D.root_cause: Checked rdm and found suction sensor not reading. Pulled shelfs to look at sensor and found sensor wire had burnt up with the heaters from defrost. Replaced sensor and checked operation. Looking at rdm found evaporator probe reading -20 and not rise or drop temp. Looked at probe and probe was also bad. Replaced evaporator probe and checked operation. Case is working cooling properly at this time.

98C06C1F-C04D-4CA3-BC83-4C81F7B2F624.root_cause: Found relay not switching over causing fans to run all the time. Replaced relay and checked operations. Case temp is back down to single digits.

9624C429-AF56-41B1-91DE-D4DB7188C157.root_cause: MT Compressor #2 tripped on breaker. Megger test confirmed internal short to ground. Compressor is failed and requires replacement.

943C54BF-A5D8-488A-AFBF-BA64DDF696FD.root_cause: Rack A high head pressure. Rack running at 300 psi. Checked condenser found 5 of 10 fans not running. (2) have broken blades, (3) had burned up wiring. Replaced blade and repaired wiring on motor #5. Motor #7 when i tried removing bad blade, lots of play in motor shaft. BAD bearings. Found split valve energized. E2 is calling for split disabled. Checked relay, its not correct one mis labeled. Need to trace wiring and find correct board and point. Temporarily just cut and capped wire to solenoid coil. All rack A compressors going off on oil failure. Confirmed oil separator was working properly. Added 3 gallons of oil to the rack. One sight glass floating in reservoir. Searched for oil leak but found none. Low oil level likely caused by refrigerant leaks overtime that have since been repaired. Compressor 3 head cooling fan not working. I took it apart and found damaged power wires. I repaired the wires. Fan is working now. Compressor 5 will not run. I checked operations and found Tim delay relay not working properly. New relay will need to be ordered. I manually ran the compressor by pushing in the contactor. Amps were high and it sounded bad. It will need to be diagnosed when the new relay is installed. Found small oil leak on compressor 3 fitting. I was able to fix this leak by tightening the fitting. Rack oil level is good. Both compressors are pulling good amps. Compressor 5 went off on high head pressure without any indication of actual high pressure. I tested the high pressure switch. It appears to be going bad. Also, all other compressors have newer style oil sentronic. Compressor 5 has old style and it is in bad condition. Recommend replacing both. Identified Rack A with the high discharge trip alarm. Noticed discharge pressure was very high with all fans being called for. Upon checking the condenser I noticed the fans were not running but 1 of them. Checked all control power connections to the contactor for when the RO board was calling for the fans. Noticed connections were loose. Adjusted connections and did a pull test to ensure they would not come loose anymore. Found leak on Hot gas solenoid valve. Repaired stem and installed cap , all sealed. No more leak.

F1924156-B1AD-44F2-8DCA-B1D4BC4E8F92.root_cause: Found (1) seized fan motor for bakery freezer.

FCF17A8C-EF1D-41A5-814A-8E99F8E1601B.root_cause: Found compressor two not in a call. Attempted to get online by switching Y2 with Y1, compressor started but did not stay on for long, pressures are good. Need to troubleshoot why compressor two is not being called for at the board.

25A4E373-D97E-41CB-B584-EFE4A67F8679.root_cause: Found leak @discharge header Schrader valve. Found valve core loose and tightened.

9D94BE0C-C5E6-4ADF-869C-47A3EE2D89EF.root_cause: Found small leak from the packing of the liquid line service port. Tightened packing and replaced gaskets to eliminate leak. Added 15lbs of R404a, from recovery jug on site, to bring liquid level and pressure back to normal. The service valve is bad (will not full isolate port) and leaking at (9999+ppm). Went to truck and got parts. Installed a dual port swivel Tee to the access port along with a purple flaremate. Leak checked again and leak is fixed (0 ppm). Found the condenser fins were bent over in a large section on the coil. Used a fin comb ;slowly and diligently straightened all fins to get better air flow. Shined a light through it the coil and couldn’t see any light through it. Next stretched out hose and cleaned coil found it was packed in the middle with debris. Cleaned thoroughly till water coming out was clear. I added 12lbs of R404a to system F01. We now have a full column of liquid going to the evap.

CA528C4F-5B06-490A-A10D-9D7A4CE42B2A.root_cause: Found door with both male and female connectors burnt up and arcing, pulled door off and replaced the male plug and re wired it, female end I had was too small, pulled out broken burnt connectors out of the female plug and put the door back in place and re connected plugs, door heater is working for now and not sparking anymore, female plug needs to be changed since it’s damaged.

A1791403-174D-4F5D-8E9A-6766702EE3D5.root_cause: Found transducer reading way off, put in temp offset to get rack online.

191DB16A-BDA5-4618-ADB4-BAAB74567E53.root_cause: Found liquid line service valve cap leaking tighten/backseated service valve and replaced cap and leak stopped.

1B908104-4DD9-46C8-BD12-6E180F78AABD.root_cause: The coil is starved and I think there’s a restriction in the cap tube. Found restriction on cap tube, found cap tube too long.

29C5D94E-32D4-472F-9B91-C3A08C8968C1.root_cause: Found the right side evaporator’s TXV equalization line going into the suction header had snapped off and was actively leaking. The leak was caused by a fan blade that lost its fin and was causing the whole unit to shake violently. Repaired leak on evap, brought box back online and traveled to Stockton WH to pick up refrigerant from Safeway stock. Charged 200# of reclaimed r507a to rack LT-A upon return. Will need to return next week to replace broken fan blade and follow up leak check. All circuits are at temp and out of alarm. Found the last circuits on the liquid header on rack LT-A to be intermittently hightemping. Rack is still low from leak found yesterday. Topped off rack with 200# of reclaimed r507 for previous repair made on dispatch 2-1792207. All cases are now at temp and sightglass is clear. Conducted leak check, no further leaks found. Checked in and waited for product to be moved from the front of the evaporator in the GWIF to gain access to fans. Replaced the broken fan blade and verified unit is no longer shaking.

699291DE-A149-4579-B27D-A5B4DBA16084.root_cause: Found a leak in the service deli system 40-2. Pumped down the system and repaired the leak on the outlet of the evap coil. This is just a temporary fix and there's a pass cut out of the coil, the coil needs to be replaced, this isn't repairable.

3FB0842E-D31C-436C-8A2B-13351EA1662B.root_cause: Verified thermostat has failed by positioning temp bulb of a new thermostat in the same location as installed thermostat. New thermostat switch opened while installed thermostat stayed closed. Removed and replaced failed thermostat.

2E1BD84A-9736-49FE-8218-CD8B3AE9A8A3.root_cause: Found the cause of the vfd overheating to be a defective exhaust fan in the electrical component.

0D7FD157-57F2-402F-9D83-B4BFA31AD4A5.root_cause: Found contactor melted, isolated. Replaced bad Contactor and replaced bad wire also, all the compressors are now running and cycling off.

ABDD1039-9A7A-472A-85D7-8C2A252F93DD.root_cause: After inspection of case I found TXV not functioning properly. After pumping down circuit and disassembly of TXV I found that the cartridge was completely caked with debris and needle in cartridge unable to move.

06E9A1B3-CDD5-4DCB-A3FE-267C090E3805.root_cause: Found drain line for walk in freezer damaged outside of the box. Pipe was cracked and seems like someone hit it with a pallet. Cut out damaged section of pipe and welded in a coupling. No other issues found and pipe is no longer leaking.

CAB89662-85B6-4854-ABB9-4893C8CF7140.root_cause: Found condenser fan motor failing intermittently. Found rub out on control hose to pressure switch. System was not engaging due to thermostat remaining open and when lowering set-point found low pressure cutout open due to rub out. Repaired rub out on liquid line. Removed compressor and tilted over to remove oil and pumped in oil till sight glass was half full. Replaced dual pressure safety. Replaced liquid line drier. Replaced txv and power head. Pulled vacuum. Replaced condenser fan motor and thermostat. Set dual pressure switch. Vacuum pulled under 500 microns. Charged system with 10 lbs of r448a. Set superheat to 3df.

0D3A0D43-7D5E-4403-853E-12443350F526.root_cause: Found oil on A8 valve. Rebuilt valve, pulled vacuum. Opened valve to allow pressure, shut valve and tested with leak detector, bubbles and allowed time to pressure test. No leaks detected. Added 10lbs 404a. Monitored multiple ice cycles to ensure proper operation. Unit is operational.

E4FD5457-C5F5-444D-ADD1-9EF08C79B975.root_cause: found bad time clock holding unit in defrost.

131B67A6-51A5-45D9-85DD-778438E04559.root_cause: Further diagnostics determined the defrost controller had failed, preventing proper defrost operation.

464BBDFE-D78C-4A10-97E0-FCDC6D9F0059.root_cause: I traced out and found an open controller above the wetrack. I removed and replaced the controller and reset.

7687B326-4B21-4DD4-8A3F-89282A5BE78F.root_cause: Found 2 leaks at the bottom right side of coil. Pumped down coil, recovered remaining gas back into rack. Brazed leaks, pressure tested coil, and vacuumed. Turned system back on, sub cooler alarm is still cleared. No need to add more gas. Job completed

29C05AEE-8BAE-421E-8F20-53472956249B.root_cause: Flare fitting from subcooler to interstage leaking over 700ppm and oil dripping from fitting.

5E8D4754-1191-4DF4-B808-406CB0B19B19.root_cause: Replaced plugged liquid drier in case 10B.

8F0666EF-9C21-4D48-A96C-8F6A11D121FC.root_cause: Found that one fan is dead and the other one is spinning weak. Replace both fan motors.

8BBE03C7-DAB3-4DCA-A1AF-9538F19EBA1C.root_cause: Found that the old drier was completely clogged. Found blown fuse in the case controller, replaced fuse with new one from a spare controller on site. Investigated pulse valve wiring and found a wire that rubbed through, repaired this.

2CFC8628-2D1B-4226-9609-42A7C4C320EE.root_cause: I noticed iced buildup at bottom of Evap. coil & left side fan motor seized up. I replaced bad motor.

AE060C78-94CB-4A76-985D-1C8AA2E141FF.root_cause: Cleaned TXV screen- it was extremely dirty

861174DE-2B77-4950-8709-28DD24CECF91.root_cause: On arrival no airflow. Pulled product center section drain full of ice and all other sections drain clear but lots of frost on front of coil. Store pulled all product and Deiced case. After deicing. Most valves fully feeding or stuck open when it came back to temp. Watched all cases come to temp 32ab stuck at 26* tested sensor in ice water still 26* replaced sensor all sections now accurate and down below 0. Somewhat high superheat but valves are non adjustable. Replaced 5 txvs on system a34a had Chris deice cases. Replaced drain pan heater in center section. All cases pulled down to -10 and are no longer stuck wide open

39D461CF-059C-4957-9310-619EBDAB6175.root_cause: Fan motor is seized. Plug in port for the fans is worn out and the daisy chain will need to be replaced. Found that 3/5 fans were not operating. Removed fan covers for fans 3 and 4 found both motors seized.

AB80C8D4-035B-475F-9BF6-0EB8ACCF7F4D.root_cause: Rack 3 receiver gauge gasket is leaking.

D72B4903-3ECD-4864-9B01-64BD46325C0F.root_cause: Compressor was not running and was hot to the touch. Take top off unit and verify compressor out on internal overload. Check run capacitors on condenser fan motors and found them weak. Inspect condenser fan motors and found play in shaft, replace both condenser fan motors. Check temp drop across driers no temp drop found. Sight glass has some bubbles moving through but not flashing, sub-cooling is around 30 degrees.

32217F45-E51B-4B67-A23E-45936A2DA3A6.root_cause: Determined the Temprite oil separator has failed. MT compressor #2 oil control issue. Oil regulator is not maintaining proper control, and OMB solenoid was observed in an open state without a call for oil while sight glass indicated full.

19656440-CAB8-4018-AC98-0D5E012DCF88.root_cause: Found leak on A9 pressure regulator hooked up to receiver. Found housing is leaking. Tried tightening the 4 bolts on the housing. This did not stop the leak. Isolated section with ball valve on one side and service valve on other side. Found no other leaks at the moment. Added 48lbs r404a to bring up receiver level. Need to order new A9 Flo-con valve to repair leak. Leak is isolated.

D6A233C3-426E-4A4F-9C1E-45E527D2A7B3.root_cause: I found the fan unplugged and both the female and male connector melted

423A431F-697C-4AAF-979A-76F11C0230A1.root_cause: 3 way valve solenoid is burnt and swelled up. Needs to be replaced asap. Solenoid is a ( MKCL) 120v -208-240v, 50-60 cy. 10 W

D0EC8679-D17F-4537-9E73-03659EE0F787.root_cause: Found leak on circuit A9 hot gas stem cap loose. Tighten down. Leak repaired

38FEF566-0241-404F-A101-DAABF7568510.root_cause: Replaced end of line filter, Hydrophobic Filter, and adjusted digipots as the leak detector was experiencing a clipping fault (code 8000) after adjusting and replacing parts leak detector stopped alarming

69A24AD6-170E-4EC6-BEB1-F8757A9C1C8C.root_cause: Found condenser fans were not running, refrigerant not getting cooled down at all cause for high temps/pressures. Vrf for condenser C had an earth fault error code. Shut off power and checked all terminals to ground but did not get any ground contacts. Shut off fan motor contactors coil power and reset vrf to see if it would trip on the same issue again but it worked fine. After turning controls back on, checked amperage on motors, found all motors at about 2 amps except for Motor #8 which read 4.7 amps. Removed fuses to condenser fan motor and now vrf is not tripping on ground fault. All cases came down to temp and condenser is working ok. C5 seafood service counter was not dropping temp because of bad fan motor, replaced it with truck stock evaporator fan motor. Need to order a condenser fan motor and install it on Motor 8 condenser C. Fuses are in the electrical section in front of contactors.

EC4FB67C-7C52-4486-82D0-1C39EBFA1EDA.root_cause: the Alarmed on P1 (sensor fault) then back to normal, after that controller screen started blinking, verified correct voltage at controller, replaced controller and ran new coil and room sensors, adjusted parameters and checked operations all is now normal case is at temp

801D072B-5F6F-406C-A0F7-554AEF92585E.root_cause: Cause of Failure -- Found Short Grounded

9B32BC76-5CD1-44EC-B07D-584B4AE58536.root_cause: Wire size from panel to motor is 8AWG which is too small as per motor nameplate.

2BCCDB42-DCD7-476D-B70D-498F8A248038.root_cause: Based off of the ice build up repeating and low suction pressure indicates a refrigerant leak. Leak searched the unit and the evaporator coil was the only thing that was leaking. The condenser checked out okay no leaks.

F1A46A7F-800C-42BF-A56A-F5782D890680.root_cause: Discovered that one condenser fan motor was not operating and was drawing 2.3 amps, indicating an over-amp condition. Diagnosed failed capacitors and replaced two out of the four. Also identified a pitted contactor, which was replaced at this time.

E4C4F693-E40A-4A24-9D0C-84A2565F87D2.root_cause: Found compressor 2 contactor pulled in and no amps being drawn. Killed unit and inspected compressor side connections. Found wire connections a bit rusty. Found screws on catactor a little loose. Tightened lugs. Turned on unit. Place amp meter on wires and manually pushed in contactor. Found compressor pulling LR amps at 88 amps. Killed power. Disconnected wires from contactor to prevent breaker blowing. Taped up ends. Gained all information needed for compressor replacement.

27F52184-0467-4CD5-BA5F-D1F327C2007E.root_cause: Found case at 60 fan motor out. Replaced fan motor now working.

8F3C6CB7-1B57-4201-B90F-3A1EC9273CBF.root_cause: The solenoid is intermittently getting stuck and not feeding. The old solenoid was not opening or making noise even with solenoid coil energized. New solenoid is energizing and working properly.

A31271BB-F086-4304-B46B-66D3FAC1074F.root_cause: Found powerhead no longer has charge and reached end of life.

B7D1FB5B-7E9A-4ABC-B20A-AB31A31AD48B.root_cause: Advised to change out TXVs and driers for both circuits.

F54B56DA-74DA-4273-A585-5F76E026401F.root_cause: Found compressor #2 suction line loose at the king valve.

011CFBC3-C3FA-43B7-9C20-B0C73CA8567A.root_cause: Removed panels and found 2 bad fan motors. Replaced fan motors and system came down to temp.

DE58CFD5-B2CA-40D1-B312-F6323CF8664B.root_cause: I arrived and checked in. I then installed heat tape in freezer.

27D75CCA-7429-44DC-A21A-69EC5D53FAD2.root_cause: Found the liquid line solenoid to have failed internally and cause it to not open or close properly. Also the valve body failed and is leaking.

ECF16254-CA7D-4231-8B0A-6919FB783BA6.root_cause: The pan wasn't broken, it was just the evap drain pan hook had been knocked off while stocking and unstocking case causing water to leak onto food. Removed panel and found hook inside and remounted correctly. Found axial fans under case not working and full of debris. Cleaned fans and repaired connection and fans began running. Last fan had to fully remove to clean and repair connection. All axial fans now running. Had to pick up a transflow blower motor and wire it in under case because of condensation and failed pan insulation, the cases are extremely old. Ran wire whip from electrical panel in case to fan. Fan now running. All condensation clear and no water on floor. Cleared all debris from drains with co2.

070032A9-46CD-47DE-8462-184E27AE246F.root_cause: Found fan blade broken and laying on top of condenser coil. Found the bracket for motor to be cracked as well which caused the blade to break. Removed all broken fan bracket and blades. Replaced with new and verified all fans now spinning.

AB7F0317-4FEC-497B-B895-5176E53FA5BC.root_cause: Found one of the fan motors in the case was very loud due to a bad or worn out bearing, pulled motor off of truck stock, and replaced it with a new one.

B5AFA51C-5230-4F71-B955-874B1718CA8F.root_cause: Checked case and found compressor pulling lock rotor amps.

DA5B6E7B-CF12-46E8-81C9-5C36410E4D9E.root_cause: Vacuumed the drain pipe from the outside, the trap was clogged. All of the water from the drain lines and drain pan came out. Inside the cooler, no more noise and drain pans were empty. Fan was noisy splashing the water on the coil. Also I saw a few spots on all 3 drain lines not having proper grade and I fixed that. Added 2 missing clamps on the drain pipe.

B2FE9D24-8209-4027-85E9-21010F7DE7E2.root_cause: Noticed that water was not draining. Exposed drain with hot water but nothing was draining. Got my shop vac and started cleaning out drain line. Took a few tries but got drain clear. And a lot of dirt and gunk what caused drain line to clog.

73550E4B-DE0D-493E-A1F5-BBF74EA17C70.root_cause: Found Börgen wine s/c case freezing wine and compressor running nonstop. Removed and replaced Dixell case controller, set up all parameters and tested multiple times. All ok on departure.

28B8A937-CC5B-4F6B-8882-9BEF16859759.root_cause: Upon inspection I observed the low pressure switch to be open. I checked and found the pressures to be higher than normal. I located a new pressure switch from truck stock. I removed and replaced the faulty pressure switch. I observed the unit to operate properly.

8CD20860-B574-4FC4-894D-C2CC361DA469.root_cause: I found three motors that were not spinning. The motors were internally damaged.

BF2EFB09-0EB8-4ADD-BDD2-D6E81679006C.root_cause: Found Cases running warm due to high super heat, found pressure drop of 50 PSI acrid liquid line filter driers, pumped down and replaced filter drier, found filter drier service valve to be leaking, will be returning with replacement service valve.

BAE8B856-8BC6-45AC-8A6B-B7166441CDEE.root_cause: Found possible leaks on piping underneath service meat case system B 12 B. Main leak is coming from Schrader core on liquid line on same case. Found TXV leaking from cap. Added nylog and tightened to fix leak.

F060E8DB-AFB2-4F8C-A39B-D1BBEA5AB8FE.root_cause: Replaced middle right evap fan motor due to evap fan motor binding

670305FE-E658-4977-8DCB-088441798DE1.root_cause: dual pressure switch open bad switch

ABD56CC2-B38D-46B6-956F-E3121DC2AEB7.root_cause: Inspected drain pan pipe heater & it is not working causing drain to ice up.

CA3D2EAE-2A5E-4278-8DED-F727CE0188AB.root_cause: Compressor was unwired and disconnect is off. Verified compressor is bad. Found a bad OMC coil control. Found a very small leak coming from the discharge line service valve.

13362621-B7A3-40CB-9680-A201286B52E6.root_cause: Found all the cases controllers are forced close. Check the case controllers and all of the cases controllers. Lost some parameters like Freon and types of transducers. While I was doing that Dave from Danfoss controls tech support find that the cases controllers are not blocking to receive the data. So he pushed the data in a small groups of cases and programming the case controllers in same time. Override compressor two to start pushing some gas to cases and kettle by letter all cases started feeding. Also add one bottle of liquid to rack J. Also the drives in both racks are not responding.

851CCF6E-9BDB-49C2-8942-F40FDAE67B86.root_cause: Took apart old contactor and found L3 contact burnt up

5E7831B3-9381-463F-9B5F-AD4ED9FDBF1F.root_cause: Found it to be the 4D compressor module shorted. Rack E is flat on refrigerant. Will need to pressurize system with nitrogen to locate and repair leak. Then add 400 lbs of 448.

D1861878-0B35-4980-A9BA-DE0631D62EFB.root_cause: Found EEPR was showing 100% open. Reset EEPR and found temperature and pressure began dropping for circuit. Will need to order new EEPR for circuit. Located replacement valve and picked up. Returned to store, pumped down a valved off circuit. Recovered remaining freon back into the rack and removed the faulty valve from the system. Installed new valve, put system into a deep vacuum, pressurized, leak checked work and returned system to service.

2965AC68-40F2-4204-B56A-47070E7F5153.root_cause: Found oil leaking from comp3 oil rotolock fitting.

819A4BDB-EBA9-41C0-9197-C23A93458748.root_cause: The 45 min defrost was almost 60 min and temps were at 60*

4C6B21D6-E14D-40D0-9B89-53DFA7C3153D.root_cause: Troubleshot system and found the cond coil dirty and the cond fan motor failed. Brushed off coil and replaced cond fan motor.

9D6A3C2C-14B8-453C-85AE-AEE3AF3F3125.root_cause: Upon inspection found faulty harness outlet causing motor not to run. Removed old motor harness. Installed new motor harness.

1B07722B-6755-4807-8BA6-AC0D41C24A8C.root_cause: Replaced all 4 contactors. One of the auxiliary’s was bad, swapped it out from one from my van. Had to rewire the connections on the new auxiliary.

3F697744-7739-43BA-B281-39330E81DB11.root_cause: Found discharge transducer to have failed due to a brief power surge at 6pm.

CB1F1577-4449-4555-8098-9FD227239E06.root_cause: I then removed and replaced the fan that was out in deli case D06-C with one from van stock.

4E0E88AE-438D-4E96-B6D9-EF037C32A1DD.root_cause: Found a leak on suction valve rotor lock.

78F75942-4B45-4779-9B26-2EAA588FF583.root_cause: checked fan that was running clockwise and all others were running counter clockwise as that motor was recently changed but it was a counter clockwise only motor and has gone bad reversing polarity internally

CA8F679D-8979-451F-A24F-B4FF368DAA40.root_cause: Found end fan to be unbalanced and has blown bearings . Replaced with new motor verified spinning correct direction . Still slight viberate on had to resecured fan blades and tighten guards unit is now operating normally And is quiet

3748BEDE-8AC8-47CD-82AC-0D25BF3F1645.root_cause: Found power to fan but motor internally faulty . Replaced with new motor .

9C28939F-4E31-4AF7-9B37-26D199D9B9C7.root_cause: Compressor five and six have bad Reeves and plates. Compressor five and six have bad Reeves and plates. Found broken reed valve on all heads. Top head plates could not be changed due to the wrong plates but changed reed valves.

33A2F72C-991E-4514-93B6-1F1D00D811AE.root_cause: Found the override rocker switch for the fans set in manual and the 4 evaporator fans failed. Replaced with 4 fans from truck stock and cords. ( 43602 and 41664 ) programmed motors for 1200 RPM. Also found the rocker switches in manual for B5A,B and C. Those fans are operational. Placed rocker switches to auto operation so the fans shut off during defrost cycles. There is a a lot of ice build up on the shelves in B5B. Made Andrew the FF manager aware that he should de ice those no later than Monday. Spoke with Kenny and Gerry, the third door where the sensor is has restricted air flow from ice on the coil. Came out to site to follow up and finish repairs from over the weekend. Upon arrival checked in with Dave, he said the beer, dairy, and the produce walk-in was still not working. Isolated the evaporator to 0psi and began to sweat out the old drier. Placed a new drier in from truck stock and welded it securely. Found moisture inside valve, evacuated evaporator and restarted condenser, noticed that new drier was plugged again, isolated evaporator again and removed drier, piped TXV straight since condenser already has a liquid drier and there was no pressure differential across it, recovered all 43 lbs of 449a at condenser and began evacuating system, noticed that unit would not drop below 1600 microns, inspected oil at compressor and noticed cloudy appearance, this indicated that oil was contaminated with moisture; replaced oil on compressor, sourced from truck stock, and on vacuum pump, also from truck stock, and restarted evacuation. Unit does not pull to the 500 microns so will leave vacuum overnight. Unit is still down, placed sensor override for 24 hours to avoid alarms. Will return tomorrow to recharge into with virgin refrigerant. Call not complete. Found suction filter plugged up; removed and replaced filter & evacuated evaporator all over again, system began to pull down to temp normally until it reached 5°f box temp. New suction filter got restricted again, performed oil acid test and resulted in positive for acid in system, will return to site to recover new refrigerant again, install two suction ball valves for accumulator and piping isolation, so that pressure build up can push out all remnant contaminated oil in piping and evaporator coil, replaced suction filter and liquid drier, flush out and clean accumulator, and recharge unit with virgin refrigerant again. WIF is down again. Recovered 47 lbs of 449- A. Once all pressure was zeroed out we began to unsweat liquid line filter and suction filter that were clogged due to moisture in the system. Flushed unit with RX-11 throughout the entire system and blew it out completely with 150psi of nitrogen to ensure all moisture and any debris was out of the system. Added new filters and brazed them in securely. Began to pull a vacuum and verified it pulled down to 500 microns. After the vacuum was complete we broke the vacuum ensured all hoses were purged before charging up the system. Added 42lbs of 449-a into the system. Started to monitor the unit pull down after the refrigerant charge. Adjusted superheat accordingly. Superheat maintaining 5 degrees upon departure. Unit at setpoint.

She said they are getting a remodel soon and only want the fan replaced. Checked out with Erica 1630. Store keeps leaving door open causing unit to high temp. Tested operation and verified the fan was running properly with no obstructions or contact with wiring. Unit is operating normally at this time.

C5861C52-29A1-40D8-9338-C1996E1685AA.root_cause:
Sys 2A5 WI Bakery Freezer: took a look at defrost operations & found that freezer terminated defrost on a time of 30 minutes. The way the outputs are wired the evap fan & refrigeration solenoid are energized at the exact same time. This means there was no fan delay after turning the refrigeration circuit on. Noticed there was a defrost termination probe in the evap coil, with a broken wire, that was not being read by the E2. Replaced wire & set it up in the E2 to be read as 2A5 defrost termination temp probe. Set defrost to terminate on a defrost termination probe temp of 52 degrees. Set minimum defrost time to 10 minutes & max time to 30. Lowered the number of defrosts a day down to 4 a day from 6 a day. Since there is no evap fan delay & I couldn’t program one in the E2 due to the way the fan & refrigeration solenoid are wired I installed a fan delay klixon on one of the legs of power for the evap fan. Got freezer running and verified fan delay klixon delayed fan until coil got cold enough. Turned door frame heater breaker back on & verified operation of door frame heater. Verified operation of drain line heater. Box still pulling down to temp when leaving call. Box temp to be monitored tonite for any issues. Leaving call open to readdress how box defrosts & make any changes if necessary.

Returned to check defrost on bakery walk in Freezer. Relocated termination sensor from suction header near heater to front side of coil spaced between heaters. Defrost is working as it should. Sealed penetration on top of box where sprinkler comes through. Spray foamed any penetrations I found. All ok at this time.

482840BF-4D9B-42DF-B8D7-065C4773CFFE.root_cause: I found one fan out in case 2.2B. I replaced the bad fan. Then I moved to my solenoid valve and EPR. I found they both had a strong electromagnetism current. I checked power and they didn’t have power going to them. I went out to the rack house to check the RIB. When I got to it said that circuit 2.2 should not be getting voltage for its RIB board under the case. I took the bottom of the case apart and had a hard time finding the board. Well the board was really just a relay. The relay wasn’t getting power (expected) and it should be send 120V from the hot fan leg to the LLSV which is in series with the EPR. The RIB relay wasn’t sending power to the LLSV. I replaced the RIB relay with a new 24V coil relay and wired the fan and LLSV to the NC terminals. The valve opened and started cooling. When I was plugging the fans back in for 2.2B one of the fan rotation wires were naked and touched the fan shroud and burned the motor up. I replaced the motor with a new one.

8EE05BB3-90CF-4DFB-84D0-A05FBB7FD9B0.root_cause: Found drop leg from condenser giving various readings. Going warm for a normal operation to extremely cold. Worked with service manager and we discovered that condenser fan motors are not cycling as programmed in Danfoss causing large swings and head pressure. Tech pumped down three cases and replaced liquid line dryers in cases. One of three cases pulled instantly to temp other two cases still having issue. Frost patterns on distributors show inconsistent flow. Tech performed as a test on rack and rock instantly failed for high moisture and acid. Advised service manager and will follow up tomorrow to attack moisture issue completely. Advised store to pull cases as needed refrigeration supervisor is aware on the supermarket side. Assisted tech with case not pulling down which we verified moisture in system. Tech responded for follow-up regarding moisture contamination in Rack E. Tech met with the service supervisor and inspected the EL9 bunker. It was determined that the case was contaminated with moisture. Techs replaced the case filter driers and valve stems. Upon pulling a vacuum on the bunker, techs found the system to be heavily contaminated with moisture. The bunker was placed under multiple vacuum pulls to remove moisture. Rack filter driers were also replaced, and the rack was pulled into a vacuum. The bunker was left under vacuum overnight to further remove moisture from the case and associated system components. Tech will return to reopen the bunker to the system and replace the rack driers again to ensure proper moisture removal. System was left under vacuum at the time of departure. Tech responded for follow-up on moisture issue on Rack E. Upon arrival, tech found the system in vacuum at approximately 775 microns. Tech removed the vacuum pump and reopened the system. Tech monitored operation and verified temperatures were dropping. Tech inspected the EL7 cases, which had recently been filled, and noted slightly elevated temperatures while monitoring. Tech waited until the EL9 cases reached negative temperatures and then placed them into defrost to verify proper recovery after defrost termination. Tech placed the liquid line to the rack drier section into bypass and pumped down the rack drier core. Rack driers were replaced, and the rack drier section was then pulled into a vacuum. After achieving proper vacuum, tech reopened the drier section by closing the bypass and opening the inlet and outlet valves. Tech monitored system operation and verified the EL9 case came out of defrost and pulled down properly. EL7 cases were also verified to be operating in the negative range. System was operating properly at the time of departure. On continuing follow up to store to examine rack after high moisture content. Replaced liquid line cores again replaced oil filter as well as performing acid test. Acid test did finally pass with full completion. High moisture liquid line core still in rack to be replaced on upcoming p.m. with standard cores. Currently no alarms at rack and all cases at temperature.

Needs 12 30-amp 3-pole 240V coil contactors. The main store AC is not running. Reset the thermostat alarms and the VFD. Reset condensing units. All store ACs are running. The bakery freezer is warm. Found the leak alarm is off. Unhooked the sensor wire, and the unit is running with no alarm. Tech has a new sensor ordered. The original quote was based on the initial inspection with the assumption that no follow-up work or additional material would be required. Once onsite, the scope expanded due to conditions that weren't confirmed until power was restored and a full review of the equipment could be completed. During the visit, technicians were required to inspect multiple refrigeration units affected by the outage, verify operating conditions, and confirm that no hidden issues existed. In addition, parts usage exceeded the quote due to the actual on-site condition. Some components expected to be reusable or within tolerance were not, prompting us to replace said parts to return the equipment to normal operation. These parts were required to complete the work correctly and avoid repeat service calls. The additional labor and parts were unavoidable, but of the field conditions that were not visible or verifiable at the time the quote was created. All work performed was necessary to complete the request and ensure the equipment was left operating properly following the outage.

I also checked if there was a full column of liquid through the sight glass. I took a pressure reading of the EPR valve, which was at 35 psi. This resulted in a saturation temperature of 13 degrees, making the coil too cold for the walk-in cooler. I adjusted the pressure to 48 psi, bringing the saturated temperature to 25 degrees and getting the coil temperature to the desired medium temperature. I pumped down the circuit to access the mechanical expansion valve screen. Upon inspection, I found it dirty. I cleaned the screen and reinserted it. Once the system was in a vacuum, I opened the circuit. I began adjusting the SH to 10 degrees. I also picked up a new time clock and installed it inside the rack. I had to wire the time clock and confirm its operation.

C04ACCE7-4D2D-44C7-900E-599DA2E31704.root_cause: Removed covers and installed new fan cycling controls for condensing unit c and condensing unit d. Added 2.5# to CU to rack D and added 3# to cu rack C, both at 25%.

C3573C07-10A6-4A5E-B628-B19E2711D3AC.root_cause: Heaters were pulling full amp draw, unit has 2 heaters. Filters in unit hadn’t been replaced since July. And thermostat had a bad connection.

77AC3112-1AF4-4D6C-AD52-FC89580D1C58.root_cause: Faulty EFM in produce replace with one in van inventory adjusted RPM on motor as required.
