Torched the refrigerant receiver and it was at the bottom. Added refrigerant to the system. The sight glass cleared up. Torched the receiver and it was at about 50% , and I went down stairs to check the box temperature, it was at 36 degrees.

F917A7CA-8E0D-477A-A90A-4EF67827FEF6.root_cause: Findings support diagnosis of a faulty control board as the root cause.

37AAE381-380C-49DF-97E8-DD773C74C5A2.root_cause: Removed bad sensor , installed new sensor . Controller reading sensor and out of alarm .

C6249C42-CEB6-467D-92EE-9DE43028810E.root_cause: Found leak on comp B1 fitting. Found additional leak on liquid housing shell.

03E8880A-24ED-4C3F-933B-715608F3B607.root_cause: Found compressor 5 on rack A in oil failure. Oil is present in oil resevoir. Reset omb on comp 5 and compressor now running. Valved off oil line and made compressor trip, opened lines up and comp 5 filled. Found that comp 2 on the low temp side of rack full of oil. Omb on comp 2 is bleeding by and causing oil to go into compressor. Omb has failed. Picked up new parts from supplier. Returned on site isolated old oil filter. Installed new oil filter on rack A. Pulled vacuum-good Opened lines back up. Added tag with date of filter replacement. Rack is now feeding oil. Isolated compressor 2. Removed OlD oil control. Mounted and wired new OMB. Pulled vacuum on compressor-good Made omb trip on oil failure, then opened line to watch fill. Compressor is now filled. All compressors on rack a are now operating. Suction is at setpoint. This call is complete. Checked out with manager on duty Alex kresena at 5:00pm

7DFBCCB2-124D-4541-972D-79BBBB99124B.root_cause: found 2 faulty evaporator fan motors. Removed and replaced fan motors from truck stock and cleaned blades. Restored and tested operation functioning as should.

46A14660-BA6B-4A2F-9082-1CE6F0A1BBC4.root_cause: Found leak on packing nut on discharge line for transducer. Tighten. Used Teflon and nylog. No more leak.

6AF14830-93B6-4510-B5C4-F68F10172BBF.root_cause: Found leak on liquid service valve for B08 was able to tighten packing to stop leak, found that there was a leak on ball valve for condenser, I was able to take off cap and Teflon and nylog tightened down and leak stoped, also found that the manual stem was leaking on B07 liquid line solenoid, back seeded stem and tightened cap.

839C14D7-EF8E-46D9-950A-06C57B2E9E05.root_cause: Found separator filter exposed and deteriorated. Found a lot of debris build up inside separator and a lot came out when float was removed , float was severely clogged. Found separator filter exploded sending its glass silica fiber throughout entire rack oil circuit, dropped oil float and found separator holding approximately 2 gallons of oil. Cleaned separator with degreaser and shop vac, installed new filter for separator and OFE1, and new float assembly, pumped in 6 gallons of oil, evacuated isolated suction and discharge headers down to 150 microns, restarted rack, noticed that float assembly clogged again; pumped down rack and repeated steps, dropped float once again and evacuated again. Restarted rack, monitored temps get close to set point, float assembly clogged up once again. Repeated all steps. After cleaning new float for a second time, repeated steps and restarted rack. Rack began reaching set point along with all circuits.

DD292CDE-E25A-4246-976E-A8B602E07489.root_cause: I found there was a pin hole leak on the outlet. I repair the bad joint and pulled a vacuum on the system. I recharged the system with recovered refrigerant. I had removed 32lbs of F448A. The system start up charge was 35lbs. I added the remaining 3lbs of R448a from my truck stock. The site glass is clear. I installed the new fan cycling control and set the pressure. The fan kicks on at 195 - 200psi and and cuts out at 135 - 140psi. I leak checked the unit / cases and had no leaks. This job is complete

23A42C7F-0233-4270-9011-178885F22490.root_cause: I found a leak on rack A on compressor number two on discharge pressure control. I went ahead and removed head pressure control and brass fitting. Used nylog on threads and placed onto compressor and tighten down. Cracked liquid line and leaked check on brass fitting. Found NO leaks. Used leak detector & bubbles no leaks. Placed high pressure switch on fitting with nylog tighten down part. Leaked check again after and found NO leaks.

E75EEC58-EAB5-4C38-97D6-D9C2C7DBF844.root_cause: Found a leak on the port of the discharge king valve

I cleaned the oil sensor. Compressor is staying on now. Oil pressure is good.

F8D8DE24-54DB-47CE-95BC-275F78926F31.root_cause: Found compressor 3 shut off with a note that comp has horrible internal rattle . Noticed comp 3 had oil feed line open still. Comp three is full of oil which is what is causing other comps to not get enough intermittently.

93BA3BA4-720C-4061-834E-F41ACF78AF58.root_cause: Latch to walk-in-freezer lost a screw and it was stripped so we couldn't reinstall it.

85F82AF1-A291-436A-ABEB-0A7C64C7BFFB.root_cause: Found oil stacking in condenser due to head pressure being set too low, made adjustments to condenser strategy and and monitored for duration of time on site, was able to get oil to return to separators/reservoir. Also found rack to be low on refrigerant located. Leak on discharge service valve tightened packing made corrected. Added 300# of R407A. Followed up on call and found shaft seal on MT 1 was leaking an excessive amount of oil. Located new shaft seal kit and scheduled with store to return at 9pm to pump store down and isolate compressor for repairs. Removed damaged shaft seal kit from MT one and installed new, Pulled vacuum on comp and insure oil leak was repaired.

3B313EC5-2534-45E4-B9EE-754798856A40.root_cause: Picked up available reclaimed R507 and charged rack.  Rack needs more refrigerant.  Pumped down cleaned screens (they were dirty) started back up still not feeding, pumped sound and dissassembled valves on case 3 found pin stuck cleaned valve , re assembled.   Cleaned valve two same stuck pin.  Could not get pin out of valve case 1.  Replaced valve.  Evacuated and started.  Valves now feeding.  Pumped down store replaced driers do to dirty system.  Picked cases now pulling down, there is times when they starve and warm up.  We need more refrigerant. 50-100#.  Will ordered and follow up asap. Wax buildup maybe from high temps during summer, we may need de superheating. Picked up refrigerant, performed leak check, no leaks identified, topped off refrigerant charge with additional 75# Reclaimed R507, raised liquid level alarm set point and reduced time delay.   Getting flood back from 3B meat and 3C. Rear loader dairy. Found 1 valve flooding in each adjusted.  Job complete.  Advised customer that liquid level alarm may need further adjustment. .    If we get alarms with in the next week.  If not we are good.

49A6E5F6-A040-4AA7-871E-671A422F985D.root_cause: Compressors 1 and 3 are grounded and comp 4 is blowing high to low. Also performed oil acid test on rack oil. Oil test failed almost immediately. acid is caused in system due to electrical failure of compressors.

63AD6FAF-77A3-4A66-9CEC-D72E994917A1.root_cause: case display temps and case sensor were reading very far off, looked at sensor and saw broken wires, got replacement sensor off of truck and replaced, once replaced temps instantly dropped

4A7B686B-046A-4748-8088-58573F7C6DAD.root_cause: We had to add service ports to the system in order to work on it. This is a modification to the system and shows that the propane leak was most likely where they pinched the line set instead of brazing from the factory.

64D8B245-7BCF-40D9-BCD2-7972324CF8C8.root_cause: found blown fuse preventing fan from operating

6F9394DB-162D-4A40-8BCE-AEE905B277F9.root_cause: Leak coming from epoxy joint on evap coil. Unit flat on arrival. Replaced evaporator coil. Not leaking, mechanical failure.

6921EF77-07E7-4290-AD7C-7FE44D49FB38.root_cause: I found that the contactor had a bad point on it and was not passing the power to the comps.

B6D6A8E6-E4BD-45F3-9583-926808B5E49F.root_cause: Found 23 degree differential across filter drier on Evaporator 1; and found 10 degree differential on Evaporator 2

3AE975CC-30DE-463A-A367-187539862798.root_cause: Took cover off and found that a plastic bag got caught in fan blades causing fan to break and made fan motor get off balance. Removed and replaced fan motor with closest match possible due to this oem motor not being available.

4ED0C7F4-C80D-43EA-B34A-E78B15095EBA.root_cause: Checked in with maintenance manager located the case one middle evap motor not running removed installed new evap motor mounted and wired and checked operation ok , the cases at temp cycle off 16 f

4F061670-23A6-4AEA-894C-5B532E41F9BE.root_cause: Found issue with variable speed compressor running and then taking a long time for the other compressors to turn on to assist Suction pressure going from 39psi to 85psi before turning on and back ff compressors. 91C05F0D-9991-41BD-9D5F-1D6340CA4968.root_cause: Removed leaking 1/4" desuperheating loop rapped around discharge header.

58C503D6-C7D8-4B1B-8938-EF9E8E531BF4.root_cause: Compressor 2 was not engaging due to a failed contactor and auxiliary contact.

18AFEB36-12D1-4C41-8AB1-BCA7217F70D1.root_cause: Found comp tripped on oil. Reset and checked net oil pressure. Found rack low on oil and contactor contacts in poor condition. Replaced contactor and charged 1 gal Poe to rack.

8965E9FE-CFD1-488E-86DE-6BAD595ADFDA.root_cause: Upon further inspection found a bad time delay relay.

Vacuumed and opened system to place back in service. Added 75 lbs 407A. Replace evaporator coil in the service deli case. remove coil and install new coil. Braze coil in. Pressurized to check for leaks. Vacuum and place back in service.

7D08BC75-A74E-4EE9-982C-5F8F02F82DCE.root_cause: Found same issue with lost coil power and traced back further to find failed Main control board. Board not completing signal when cooling is being called for.

25C986D5-0A22-4C56-82E3-EDEE303865D2.root_cause: I replaced the fan motor with EC5414E.

8B4B7E1E-8C76-4E36-AEF5-49B6F8464CB4.root_cause: Found the temp sensor to be faulty. Replaced the temp sensor.

6EE55E7E-86DF-4D1C-84F0-C045E9F0DBCB.root_cause: Found failed display temp sensor on both 3c coffin cases.

EE6F25E9-C264-43E5-BD7E-477C65ADFCB0.root_cause: Pulled fans and found right evap turning at half speed.

D96CCDBF-DF97-4AA1-88E1-D538B6D6ED23.root_cause: Located one leak on Rack 1/2 on a liquid line solenoid valve. Pumped System 1B down and replaced the solenoid valve. 40A9DE57-4595-4537-80D4-9D26E0DA90BB.root_cause: Found that coil was separated from refrigeration system.

Found frozen water droplets and staff placed buckets under the coil to catch water. Both sides of the coil were not iced up and box temp was at its 28° set point. Put the circuit into a manual defrost, closed the liquid line ball valve, returned to the coil and after about 10 minutes, water started leaking from the middle fan guards. Checked the drain, there was a thick layer of ice around it that was preventing water to drain quick enough. Turned the fans off, partially dropped the drain pan, and the entire pan had a layer of ice. Broke up all ice build-up, and cleared the drain line with CO2. Cleaned and mopped all ice and water spill on the floor and let the area dry before turning the refrigeration back on. Once dry, opened liquid line back up and box pulled down to set point. Checked out w/Team Lead Javier Lora & FJX @ 4:30pm Call Complete

Findings were box needs to be resealed, some of the seams are not lining up anymore, the drain pan screws were not secure for the design holes, some areas had new holes made, the drain line does not have a proper pitch, and the thread for the drain line kit was stripped out. Also had ice build up in the drain area. The minimum defrost time was just 3 minutes. The union for the drain line had a lot of tension on the thread as the piping didn’t line up well.

Removed, rotated and reinstalled shroud and connected wiring for leds and dampers. LED board was not properly aligned with plastic cover and could not see leds. Took shroud down and apart and fixed the board placement to align LEDs and re-installed. Once that was working properly we could tell it had a 99 code identifying a 4 way valve issue. Checked the wiring on both indoor units and verified everything was tight. Worked with sterling and I went to the roof to narrow down which on the 8 condensers went to the GM office and the Cash Office. Took apart each unit and attempted to troubleshoot. Checked all wiring. On cash office unit I checked the solenoid for the 4 way valve and compared ohm readings to the GM office and both solenoids were the same. Powered on cash office and verified voltage to the solenoid and plugged it in and verified it was operating. Unit came back on and began heating the cash office. Put the unit back together. Went to GM office unit and checked board for bad points. Could not find any burn marks or bad components. Put unit back together and went back down and cash office was running properly but GM office was still showing a code 11. Began tracking down the service manual. Will return tomorrow to continue diagnostic on GM unit and fix the leak on the fresh unit.

Valved off the relief check valve on top of the reservoir to raise the oil feed pressure and it worked pushing whatever was plugging the oil filter out and we are now feeding oil to the compressors. Ran a bypass hose around oil filter because there are no isolation valves to change it. Tried to pump down rack to 0 PSI suction and removed cap tube replacing it with a hard cap to stop leak but something is bleeding pressure by and an oil shower was taken. Needless to say the oil filter will not be able to be changed like this. We need to quote to install isolation ball valves all over this rack so it can be serviced. Found the bypass hose is not big enough to move the needed volume of oil to feed the compressors. Pressurized the oil outlet to push oil to the machines and cleaned up the oil mess from yesterday. Found 3 leaks during clean up. Liquid ball valve leaking at braze joint. Super hose rubbed through on pressure switch and solenoid valve leaking at bonnet. Pumped down rack and isolated all oil floats. Closed all suction service valves and was able to get the suction to 0. Could not get the pressure off the oil line due to the failed comp 4 having a bad discharge service valve. Removed packing nut and cleaned out the body where the packing is. Re-packed with teflon rope and lubricated stem and let soak. Exercised stem and was able to get full movement and close the service valve. Comp 4 is now completely isolated. Replaced oil filter, brazed leaking ball valve, tightened solenoid bonnet, and replaced leaking super hose on compressor 4. Cleaned up the rest of oil mess and brought rack back on line. Oil pressure is now 20 psi over suction and filling all the compressors. Adjusted oil float levels from full to 1/2 glass. Leak checked again and all ok. No more leaks present. All temps good and rack operating normal at this time. This compressor also had a cap tube on the dual pressure switch snap leaking oil and refrigerant all over the machine room. Removed flare connection and capped to stop leak. No isolation valves for the oil system hold and the rack needs to be completely pumped down and all compressors valved off to replace this filter. This takes 2-3 hours when it could take 5 min. We need to install isolation hand valves on each compressor oil feed line and a main hand valve after the filter so it can be serviced. Also there are oil pump out lines on compressor 4 and 5 because they sit lower on the rack than the other 3. This keeps oil moving in and out of the lower compressors so they don't stack with oil. The check valves need to be replaced.

E7747E0B-FA14-4439-9D27-F47C39DB27C3.root_cause: Compressor was short cycling on low pressure. Strange frost pattern was forming from the LLS all the way to the evaps. Isolated liquid line and opened up LLS and found no obstructions. Put LLS back together. Evacuated isolated line. Adjusted low pressure switch to get refrigerant moving in the system but was still short cycling. System was sitting at about 50 psi and could not get head pressure to build. Added 25 lbs of 449A to build up pressures. Short cycled less but still struggling to build head pressure. Research ORI and ORD valve to check operations. ORI valve needed adjusted but could not adjust until it was running properly. Added another 15lbs of 449. Adjust ORI valve all the way in and allowed system to start building up pressure and compressor stayed running. Dialed in ORI valve to 185 psi and verified the ORD was working properly. Once system was up and running and building up pressure everything was working properly. I do not believe a winter charge was ever added or the ORI was properly set for low ambient conditions. Leak searched evaps, condenser, and accessible lineset and found no traces of a leak. Went to unit and found some ice building up in evap coils and T1 txv to be a snowball. Got kyvac and washed out the could. While system was pumped down, checked txv screens and saw they had a bit of dirt in them. Cleaned the screens. Put everything back together and got unit up and running again. Checked temp across filter dryer and found there to be a significant drop across both dryers. Looked in van for a replacement filters but had to go to supply house to pick some up. Got back grab everything I needed from van. Went back inside pumped down unit and trapped refrigerant in receiver sweated old filter dryer from T1 put and sweated the new one in. Put it on a vacuum and, pressure and leak tested it. Once verified it was good go unit up and running again to bring walk in back to temp.

High recommend repiping system 2 suction line from case penetration to suction header.

Replaced oil fail control.

The leaking pressure differential valve was unsweated (removed from piping). The valve threads and connections were repaired/sealed to eliminate the leak. The valve was re-installed and properly sweated back into the system. The system was then fully recharged with glycol for the second time. Technicians monitored the glycol rack and allowed sufficient time for the system to stabilize and pull down to the correct operating temperature range. Once the glycol temperature reached the proper setpoint and product zone temperatures were achieved and stable, the store was notified that the cases were ready for product loading. Upon completion of the work: The glycol rack was observed operating correctly and maintaining proper pressures, temperatures, and circulation. No further leaks or operational issues were present at the time technicians departed the site. The diaphragm had not ruptured and added a little air to the bottom side. Once I removed the hose I found schrader leaking. Replaced Schrader and then added full base charge of 26psi. Then confirmed new Schrader does not leak. The expansion tank had lost its base charge due to leaky schrader. Adjust expansion tank pressure to 17psi. Added glycol to system to reach a return of 22psi. Double checking the pressure on the bottom side of the expansion tank since previous adjustment we found pressure was low. Then decided to relieve all pressure from tank and fill glycol to monitor pressures. Once pressure did not drop any more we then sourced a new expansion tank locally and recharged the bottom at 18psi installed tank and adjusted glycol pressure. Unit is now up and running properly.

82CA8286-24D9-4CDF-AC7E-37F1BA4A50CF.root_cause: I noticed the superheat was running higher than normal settings with the EEV valve appears to be starving. This particular scenario has been found on several similar cases such as this one, whereas the internals of the valve need to be upsized.

532742A8-13F2-44F4-9A9D-8BBD1CAE6023.root_cause: Checked and found transducer no good. Had store pull bottom of doors, ran new cable and replaced pressure transducer, checked operation and all is ok at this time.

71D8E53A-18B8-4E75-892C-3E717C5CBF9D.root_cause: I did a pump down and found the pins stock and the cartridge dirty, I replace the powerhead and the blue cartridge and oil the pins now it goes up and down with no problem.

605D83C0-2FDB-41D9-AA24-AD75180823F1.root_cause: Checked oil circuit and found all reservoir sight glasses empty. Checked for a pressure drop across oil separator (want to see around 2-5#) & had no pressure drop. Bad filter. Line coming off of separator to reservoir is not hot indicating it’s not feeding. Closed off the outlet of the reservoir and monitored, it did not fill further indicating bad separator filter. Isolated separator, pumped down & replaced filter. Found comp 6 in oil failure. Oil levels good. Reset compressor. Net Oil pressure is 60 psi. Let compressor run while checking superheats at rack. Found sys14 and 15 having below 10 degrees of superheat 3ft from suction header. These cases need to be looked at and superheats adjusted as needed. Talked to store and they are going to pull the doors needed and we will return in the morning to check individual case operation. Returned to check system 14 and 15 superheats. Found multiple cases with no superheat. Adjusted superheat on all cases to average 6-8. Checked rack superheat and it is now 42 with a suction pressure of 17 and line temp of 24. Ice/ frost subsiding from compressor 8 and there is no frost on 5,6,7. All ok at this time. Assisted tech with dropping old float on oil separator and installing new float. Cleaned up oil. Pulled vacuum. Called out to clean up oil mess. Gathered materials to clean up oil mess next door at auto parts store, returned to site began cleaning up mess, after cleaning found oil leaking from bottom of float, pulled gas out, pulled oil out of rack, removed old float, installed new float, bolts for separator were stripped out and gasket was torn from factory, had to source new gasket locally and new hardware to complete this job, pulled vacuum on system, opened ball valves and discharge valves of each compressor, after turning compressors back on, line up a01 was alarming, this case had just came out of defrost and was attempting to pull down to temp, all alarms cleared at departure. On the previous call ( dispatch 1-1719290 ) , the technician got the oil separator operating and he checked the rack for flood back . No systems were flooding back at that time .

09F13682-7A53-4FF5-91A3-697B95ED4CF9.root_cause: Found alarm for high pressure. Cycled power again and found condenser motor does not turn on when compressor is running. Motor is being supplied with 204V and capacitor tested good at 20 MF.

Evacuated line set, leak checked new welds no leaks found. Re-assembled and restarted the case and made sure it is making temp.

86DE31CE-E2A7-486C-A735-EC250A1FFDB3.root_cause: The 2” close nipple/fitting that connected the trap to the outlet of the case was broken, I tried to source a replacement fitting that would allow the trap to connect to the bottom of the case, as there is only about 4” of clearance from the floor. I was unable to source said nipple/fitting, so I used a 2” PVC threaded 90° elbow to thread into the case outlet, and then adapted that to the existing 1.5” ABS pipe. The case is draining properly now, but someone will need to follow up with a 1.25” inline trap and possibly (2) 1.5” fernco fittings. I arrived on site and checked in with the MOD. I made my way to the case and installed a 1.25” inline p-trap inline with the PVC/ABS I installed last week. I tested the drain for any leaks and verified function. I also blew out the drain for good measure with CO2. Job is complete and case is plumbed properly.

DF0A7310-7CED-4F86-BFC1-3C66402CFE7F.root_cause: Found unit tripped on low pressure control. Picked up leak on discharge service valve bolts. Leak at service valve discharge. Tightened for repair to stop leak.

91377C92-B321-4D96-9DB0-008A5271F995.root_cause: Found discharge service valve packing leaks in compressors 4 and 5. Compressor 5 leak was nearly 5k parts per million. Tightened packing and corrected leaks.

8A084738-159A-4AD4-85D5-E58A9B95391B.root_cause: Their has been remodeling going on so I looked at the ems cable on top of walk in to make sure their was no break in the wire from the work being done up their. Went down to case and start tracing sensor. At first I saw that their was an old sensor that lead to the bottom of the case. After some time found that that was old wiring from a mechanical set up. That old temp sensor threw me off since I mistook it for the one being used currently. Took the honey comb out and found that the wire went to the top of the case. Got a ladder to look and top of case and I found the short. From the looks of it the wire was most likely cut from work being done on top of the cases. There was a 2x4 with a piece of sheet metal that looks like it cut the wire. Fixed short and ran a new sensors from top of case into the honey comb. Once sensor was reading correctly call for cooling came and unit came down to temp.

60A0FE66-4C1D-4B82-AF1A-B63E3E5847E3.root_cause: Found a leak at compressor 5 rotor lock on suction side and found another leak at liquid line solenoid valve going to deli walk in cooler. Tightened both and continued leak checking. Did not pick up anything else so added 75 lbs of R507a to rack A. Liquid level is now hovering between 25-35%. Job is complete.

AAC7450A-9043-4A31-A943-B6D6FA431E69.root_cause: Found a 5° offset for set point. Removed and placed at 0. Also found defrost was set for only 4 times a day. Data tag shows 6 is needed. Adjusted to 6

C644B2F4-93BB-444C-9EB5-6C6DE9E3F69F.root_cause: Compressor is bad, likely cause by failing condenser motor.

29B286FE-8098-44E3-8719-7EE72C6FB987.root_cause: I then took the case apart and found ice buildup behind the coil and in between the coil. then deice the case put the case back together and verify it was working properly, checked operations of the case and found the klixon to be bad. D5DA1E64-3D52-4DE6-A1C8-415DD2FF29D4.root_cause: Upon arrival checked in with manager and then located freezer saw that,the first fan was out in the right hand evaporator. Removed old motor and then wired up and then installed new fan motor.

C4DCC1A5-CDF9-4F4B-BF22-7D87694120F9.root_cause:

A piece of conduit with the J Box connector was placed underneath the suction line to support the line set I would assume, and the screw has rubbed a hole in the suction line. The line set will move/sway when refrigeration turns on/off.

5563CD28-BCF2-4234-9A3B-9429A98C101C.root_cause: Found txv not feeding due to extremely dirty internal txv screen, pumped down circuit and cleaned 4 txv screens along circuit 5C.

2FE0D5D2-829A-4D75-8C6D-22983A69D44F.root_cause: I then found that rear side TXV was not feeding properly. I then tried to adjust it but it would not adjust. I then changed TXV and adjusted new one.

17812349-A3D5-4EAC-A2CF-CB122E4E2018.root_cause: Found oil line running under compressor with rub thru leak. Found flare cracked on 3way valve. Isolated leak. Cut out flare and remade. Leak checked work. Comp 6 off on oil failure, reservoir empty.

AB2DC8A0-15DD-4815-8595-DD6FE3E58A8D.root_cause: found comp two had fused contactor and single phased other two compressors tripped

4F880B24-161D-4C07-A2B1-6769B53E669C.root_cause: Found control breaker tripped. Checked and tightened connections. Ohm out and found a shorted wire on the right side of the case going to the pulsing valve. Wire had rubbed on a piece of metal paneling. Further inspection found that the relay point had gotten damaged from the shorted wire. Did not have a controller in hand. Was able to find a controller in Victoria Tx. Returned with parts and installed new controller.

7B16E5D4-9B3A-417D-A07F-7158D0D5BCEA.root_cause: Found drain line with ice build up inside. No voltage to heat tape. Found tripped breaker for drain line. Reset and heat tape began to work. Teste d defrost and found leaks coming from drain line due to cracks. Removed damaged copper lines and installed with new copper lines and coupling. Found spark on end of heat tape touching copper. Possibly caused by forklift heating drain line as beams show to be bent. Installed seal caps on heat tape. All heaters working. Breaker remained on. Removed ice from fan blade. Drain cleared. Placed system back in refrigeration mode. Freezer reached proper temp. While insulating we found the short in the heater wire and capped it so it would no longer trip the breaker. I found a fan one of the evaporators that had completely iced over. I shut off power to the evaporator fans and deiced the fan. Once the fan was deiced I took off the fan blade and found the motor had been unplugged. I plugged it back in and returned power to the fans and the fan started running.

72F9D46A-808D-4D29-9B4E-E0B3AB6F2B62.root_cause: Condensate pump was defective. Replaced condensate pump with a different pump found locally. Pump was not strong enough to pump water vertically.

96A20F5C-F833-4615-A398-CB438173A35E.root_cause: I checked with the manager, went straight to produce, to case 76 in loop 3B. There was no airflow, it was running at 62°F, set point 36°F. I asked them to remove the merchandise, took off the covers, and found the coil completely blocked with ice. I climbed onto the rack, checked the E2 controller, and found the superheat value was absurdly high. The temperature sensor (Coil out, PB6) was indicating over 100°F. This causes high superheat, and the EEV (electronic expansion valve) is always fully open, causing the coil to freeze up. I replaced the PB6 sensor, using one from my truck stock, and placed it in ice water (32°F).

F537E729-1A7E-4F62-9A0A-9E1CFB160826.root_cause: Unplugged both idcm and waited about a hr and the board never alarmed. Hooked up the low temp idcm and the board alarmed. Unhooked the low temp and hooked up the med temp idcm and it alarmed. Hooked them both up and the board alarmed. Need to replaced both idcms, center tap transformer, and the com wire between the board and the idcms. Found the fsd in comm loss. Fsd was powered on. Checked the ip address it was correct. Power cycled it and was still in comm loss. Unplugged the cable on both ends and it came back in comm. And was alarming for open temp sensor. There was also no data points in the fsd. Programmed the temps back into the fsd. Found the walk in freezer term temp for coil 2 was open. Replaced the temp sensor and programmed back into the freezer application.

8DB75B8F-B0B2-4AC0-84BE-5326C829676E.root_cause: Found case cleaned and de iced by store. Replaced Left side motor and monitored to temp.

9CDF1198-2101-44EE-9227-C31C684A802A.root_cause: Rack C was alarming for high suction pressure. 3 compressors were off on proof failure. Reset the trax oil controls and they were all low on oil. Checked the turbashed and it didn’t have a level in it. Added 1 gallon of POE oil to Rack C. The oil levels in all the compressors were full now. There is now a ball floating in the turbashed. Rack C is back down to suction pressure.

79ED256E-2272-4E45-B37B-032853D07CE4.root_cause: Found that the compressor was no longer unloading when calling. Trouble shot a failed coresene module and a failed unloaded solenoid. A heating element has shorted out and burned up the wiring for the defrost heater and the termination sensor. While doing repairs we had to power down the controls circuit and after turning back on we got a comm loss error for multiflex  board 1. Trouble shot and was able to get most of it back on line minus The digital outputs which are still not communicating. Will need to order a new controller asap.

244B0774-1FBE-45EC-A28C-752AD26DDF45.root_cause: on arrival all evaporator fans were not running because the drain was clog and water froze stopping all fans blades, I use hot water to melt the ice and unclog drain with co2, after ice was melt two of the fans were not working, I replaced one but we have to come back to replace the other one, I close the hold with a cardboard, case has good airflow now.

635D2C52-E722-45A1-9754-7D85728B6CEA.root_cause: Found the case to have a broken temp sensor.

8AB41BC2-026E-4FE5-8235-3D478290407C.root_cause: Found the case still iced up in the middle and bottom of the coil. I disassembled the case and de iced it. I also found the fan plenum was not put back together correctly so i secured it as it should be. Management stated that the drain was severely plugged and that they cleared it when they attempted to de ice it. This was likely the cause of the ice up.

92351F77-1C3B-4549-A68D-33A040B067B8.root_cause: Found that the fuses for the compressor were blown.

8EF05B09-82F0-43E9-AFB8-06631017C808.root_cause: Found SH was good but had drop across liquid line strainer. Pumped down system and replaced strainer.

EF68F11D-B748-4541-91AE-081FC5F5222C.root_cause: Found melted wires and a melted relay on case needed replacement.

A9EC8E05-99AB-4C45-A2A7-5ACFA471CAB4.root_cause: Found rear heaters not working properly. Found evap coil starting to ice up so grabbed bucket with pump and de-iced evap coil. Removed and replaced rear heaters.

86A1F858-7ADE-40AB-AE0E-E4E42FAD2FE7.root_cause: Found main disconnect for the high speed motor locked out, had to cut the lock off and we tested the fuses, 2 out of the 3 were blown, ohm the motor out and found it good, replaced fuses and the air handle came on and started to heat store, heat is now working for entire store, job complete

4A3D75EF-8707-4704-8D58-282A3E6055DC.root_cause: After finding solenoid off possibly due to low SH alarm, forced loop 2 back on and allowed cases to come down to temp, after high temp alarms cleared only alarm that remained was probe fault for for seafood prep rear coil RD15a, that had a SH of 115* and suction temp of 137* , and then no longer reading anything around 4pm, quickly replaced probe and studied graphs on multiple cases as well walked cases to ensure no ice build up, will return on Monday to get with HEB EMS on case parameters

2548AE16-9ABB-4C15-BF92-A3F2A34C5504.root_cause: Found failed defrost term & fan delay switch. Replaced defrost termination and fan delay switch.

AA541F6A-DE8C-4B6A-A0F1-CC0DEBB20DD0.root_cause: Found low on refrigerant. Leak checked all of self cont case. Took evaporator section apart and found coil leaking in the middle end unrepairable .

E73BB211-151C-4060-B5A1-4A3427BF4A77.root_cause: Found a pinhole leak in the discharge line. The discharge line is heavily corroded due to its routing through the condensate pan for water evaporation.

C8E11FDB-3B55-4D31-896D-5EA6AEA0A5EE.root_cause: Found two sections of 09A with fans stuck in bottom tray panels. Found one fan damaged with bad fan blade. Replaced with new fan assembly and blade. Reset all esr boards and than found that 4 of the compressors on rack a were tripped on oil failure. Checked oil level and sight glass was empty. Added 1 gallon of poe-32 oil to rack and compressors filled with oil and sight glass is now full. Checked for leaks and found no oil leaks. 6956D2C2-F40B-482C-BEE3-9A1651A2E1F6.root_cause: I found that the discharge sensor was reading inaccurately: my thermometer measured –7°F, while the sensor was reading 5°F. I also verified that the superheat was within proper range. I observed that the distributor tubes feeding the evaporator never defrosted and remained at –1°F, confirming that the valve is leaking by. A new valve and filter dryer will be required. I removed the failed EEV and the filter drier, then installed a new EEV and new filter drier. All welds were inspected and verified to be secure. I then opened the ball valves to place the circuit back into operation and verified the case reached proper operating temperature. Afterward, I placed the system into a defrost cycle to confirm proper valve operation. The valve closed as designed, and the distributor tubes defrosted normally. I installed the new defrost probe and verified it was reading accurately.

4BA4ACEB-2A98-4A09-B201-EA3B5C009A5B.root_cause: Need to replace oil separator on rack B.

Did another leak search while on the roof on the condensing unit. I still did not pick up a leak, open the ball valve back up, continued to diagnose unit, ohm out compressor to see if the compressor was bad. Compressor working properly, checked contacter and fuses. Adjusted low pressure switch and that caused the compressor to finally stay on.  Continued to monitor the unit checked the E2, temperature was coming down -0. A follow up is needed, another tech will come out and have a look at it.  #1-1724876 TGT #2374 - Harker Heights, TX 9149538073 - BACKROOM: I01 - WALK IN BOX: TOO_WARM: RAUF_WIB_I01 OPU Walk in Freezer Too warm. I arrived to the store to look at walk-in freezer I01 that was running warm. Me too to see what the box has been doing when I arrived,  it was -1° and throughout the day before it had got down to -5°. Went to inspect the box and after looking at the distributing t tubes, I went to the roof to look at the condensing unit. The accumulator and the dryer was iced up. I checked my pressures. My low side was cycling down to -3 psi’. My high side went up as high as 143 psi, indicating a restriction. I pumped the system down and replaced the liquid line drier. Then I pulled vacuum on the isolated side of the system. I re-introduce the refrigerant to the system and my pressures were reading, the low side was cycling down to -3 psi. My high side went up as high as 143 psi. I isolated the system again and replaced the power cap. I pulled another vacuum and reintroduce the refrigerant to the system and the pressures were reading 20 PSI on my low side and 142 psi on my high side  still have a restriction somewhere my pressure are not meeting the design pressures of 45 to 50 psi on my suction on the head pressure should be 190 to 240 psi my superheat should be in between 8 and 12° a follow up is needed to replace the TXV, which is the last component that causes a restriction.

Jimmy (meijer tech) was onsite also and he determined that the txv powerhead wasnt working properly. We isolated the case and reclaimed the refrigerant out if the case. We pulled the TXV apart and replaced the powerhead. We also took the rest of the TXV apart and cleaned everything. Screen, rod and spring. It wasn’t really dirty. After putting the TXV back together, we pulled a vacuum on the case. The vacuum held. We put all the refrigerant back into the system that we recovered. We turned the case back on. We watched it run for a little while. The top and bottom meat case would not come down to temp. We worked with Jimmy on the issue. We thought that maybe the CDS valve or the ball valves under the case was working properly or broke. After a few phone calls and more troubleshooting. We found that the CDS valve was clogged with oil and wouldn’t let anything pass. We used a heat gun to warm up the CDS valve,TXV and the elbow on the suction line under the case. After a few mins the refrigerant started flowing again and both cases started to come down to temp. Both cases are now at set point temps. This job is complete. After some time I made my way to the case and bang looking into the case and came to conclusion that the power head on the TXV was bad. Jimmy had a new part so I started getting all tool and ready to reclaim the circuit to change the head and clean the TXV. After some time the case was pumped down into a recovery tank and we began replacing the head on the TXV. While I had the case empty of refrigerant I took all the inside parts of the TXV out to clean them properly. I then reassembled the TXV and pulled a vacuum on the system. After the vacuum we added all the reclaimed refrigerant back into the case and began checking superheat to make sure the unit runs correctly. Was having trouble with suction pressure and after some time we figured out there was some frozen oil on a joint restricting liquid flow. Once unblocked the case ran flawlessly with no further issues. Case is running 27 degrees. This job is complete.

8CC062D3-A729-49C8-9075-15024953EEFB.root_cause: I went to the roof and found the rack. After speaking with Emc Target and with the manufacturer we found there was a scaling problem, not allowing the proper signals to be sent. Emc sent out a signal which took down the rack after bringing the rack back up. The controller is now communicating properly and parameters are set properly and are no longer having scaling problem

Pumped down the case, changed out the valve. Old valve was original to the case. New valve is equivalent, had to repipe due to different body style. Went to parts house and picked up new valve and power head. Valve free spins not making adjustments. Had to pump circuit down several times. Tech helped finish fixing micro leaks on the piping. Case is no longer leaking from valve replacement.

68CD20EB-8CA7-4017-BAB5-3B9DD334BE7A.root_cause: Found that our compressor was short cycling on the off cycle. We will need to quote to replace 1/2” liquid line drier I was getting around 5 to 6 degrees differential across it.

3882300C-2FB5-47E4-94CB-0138124DA050.root_cause: Followed up and looked at motors that need to be replaced.

CD0A44C1-D7AE-4E11-ADC3-8D2C1B3027DD.root_cause: Found Reciever pressure line Valved off. Opened and monitored. Liquid level swing now reduced. Added 25lbs 448a to raise liquid level and leak checked store. Found no leaks at this time.

4E3D4E13-83E2-43DE-A790-A4C3DC194BB8.root_cause: Took deck pans out and found bad fan motor. fan was not spinning. Installed motor from my truck stock and plugged in. Proper air flow now in entire case.

1F2D3C53-372C-4AC3-AAFA-32B12BF94FC0.root_cause: Found case empty on bottom shelf and case at temperature. Danny pointed out to me which fan motor is no longer working and it is the far right one on case A3-b, removed old motor.

21249974-D062-4493-917F-7B0BA5839961.root_cause: I replaced the far right evaporator motor and fixed the plenum. Section now down to proper temperature.

54DACB90-53C9-4ADB-AEC0-68C9FB14B834.root_cause: Found most ice is on floor infront of an evap with fan out. Replaced fan.

7036FDC8-4F2A-44D2-A938-773CE1E286A1.root_cause: System 1b-4 has no sensor wire to the case from motor room, appears to have been removed a long time ago.

B44CA006-FE72-4D6F-A9FD-E76A4A8AA5BA.root_cause: Found both MT AND LT suction temps sensors are reading out of range. Will need to be replaced on pull through.

3C656A8E-787F-4047-89C8-1BD6EB4D815C.root_cause: Found system drier not included in parts ordered. Drove to warehouse and picked up new drier and then returned to site. Informed Area manager Mustapha and got approved to add a few extra hours labor to job and a drier. Checked temp on suction line and discharge, temp at drier, and ran a defrost. Defrost works great and watched any frost ice buildup disappear. After system turned on began checking temps across defrost solenoid and found 3* difference. It is suppose to be colder on closed side of coil and warm above room temp indicating solenoid is closed, and it was 93-96f degrees. Pinched line after solenoid and tested this theory. Temp dropped on opposite side of valve and system steadily dropped . Monitored to below zero. I believe the temp fix is still allowing Some discharge past and thus creating a difficult pull down attempt. It will maintain around zero or below until part is ordered and in for repair. Shut down unit and removed gas. Cut out part that is bad and installed new, after purging with nitrogen. Brazed new part in and added a longer process tube for next repair. Pulled deep vacuum and then charged with new 290, per data tag. Sealed system and then monitored ops. Unit will need to drop to temp and I don’t want to add more time to call. If this repair isn’t working we need to look into a replacement unit.

D4EB8E52-9A60-439C-B29B-401205A581FA.root_cause: Found after diagnosing the unit has several bad parts like the head master, the compressor is amping weak, and the condenser fan motor is amping weak.

D565CBD4-1316-4D34-98B3-E424FD4AE2F3.root_cause: I found that I had a bad fan motor that had burned up due to a piece of plastic getting stuck in the fan

A333BF85-2A06-4B95-8C15-E1B60AA6C2FB.root_cause: Found small leak at oil separator. One leak at flair and other a small leak through the gasket.

55C59EB5-A74A-4EE2-AEF3-E75E61852A09.root_cause: I found the leak and it was a good leak that was spraying so good the soap bubbles wouldn’t stay on it. I found a dry spot on one side. 44A6F343-2A08-4DAA-A6FC-78D8E839B60D.root_cause: Found low pressure control to be bad. Replaced with new and checked ops. Case is down to 34*.

51ED29ED-213D-4365-8CA1-318DC07F6B97.root_cause: Arrived on site, found 2 of 3 evap fans down on cake case. Checked voltage, which was a bit high, but that’s all across the store. Was able to source 1 of 2 fans locally, returned to site, changed fan & blade. Last fan now on order

1E7C2F3C-E348-4694-82B1-3EA67AD83622.root_cause: Changed out compressor for 2’ SCC, replaced filter drier, start components, and contractor, case pulling down to temp all good at this time

5A6222AD-0492-484E-BC8D-0ECFE562640B.root_cause: The C1 contactor for C01 fans is disconnected and its fan power wires are landed on the C-2 contactor. The c2 contactor is for box A07 fans. Sourced new contactor and fuse from supplier and replaced, moved wires back from C-2 to C-1. Fans now cycle off during defrost and door openings. Forced defrosts to clear ice from coil, verified all clear and fans shut off. Drip and refrigeration function properly. Box coming down to temp. The A07 fans are wired together bypassing its contactor c-2, it has gas defrost but keeps fans on during defrost, requesting new work order to address and repair following work week. All issues found were result of wiring errors during new system installation.

2EF1D351-9A8A-47A8-BAA4-1144FAFB5EC1.root_cause: I immediately found a leak coming from the liquid injection line for compressor 6. I confirmed leak and location. I valved off the injection line due to the significant leak. I removed the female adapter and sweating in a new one. The compressor already had the valves closed, isolating the compressor. I removed the female adapter and sweating in a new one. Then I opened up all of the valves, turned on the toggle switch and the compressor came on. I checked the E2 and no alarms were present. Also I did a leak check on all of the compressors, no leaks were found.

DBB53DE4-11CA-4F28-8BF8-4547FAB890B0.root_cause: The cases are icing up because the liquid line solenoid is bleeding by which is not allowing the cases to defrost properly. 02D30BAF-994A-4E2A-B25C-4078AA20F75C.root_cause: Leak checking and found leak at deli service. Thought it was coming from inside the case/coils but pin point it to the liquid line solenoid spraying liquid. Leak at B13 liquid line solenoid. Replaced solenoid for repair, to stop leak.

2F58A60E-2597-4B00-9606-D10B1133E4E3.root_cause:

A8458557-E459-48ED-B3B8-5157C54C944E.root_cause: While on site looked at electrical cord that was missing ground for produce case.

F86AD993-B60C-4D9B-9B92-6FC2C30D9F9A.root_cause: Found B1 pan cpc sensor showing nothing.

852B0A6A-F287-433E-B9DE-8D6165F355A7.root_cause: Found txv at coil #1 frozen solid.

5C303897-A62A-412E-BFBB-3ADF1933199A.root_cause: I replaced one sensor and made a bunch of adjustments. Rack A is now being subcooled.

0DAE809D-54E7-4D64-B722-25BE5CF094E4.root_cause:
Identified Self contained Freezer in the deli kitchen running very warm
Began to clean off the condenser coil and restarted the unit with the power switch next to the skid
Noticed floodback to the compressor with the compressor kicking on properly. Noticed it ran all the way throughout the suction
Accessed the evaporator coil and noticed that the entire evaporator coil was fully iced up with the TXV being half iced up as well
I began to check if the evaporator fans were operational and both evap fans next to the coil on top of the unit were completely out
These faulty fans have caused floodback to the compressor and they are not allowing the unit to get into the negatives
I began to check wiring and power to the fans and noticed there was missing power
I found 3 burned out wires one of them directing to the evap blower
Upon checking the sensors the control temp sensor had a 10 degree differential in iced water reading 44 degrees
I replaced this sensor and it began to read properly on the controller
Noticed the unit began to pull down below freezing (32F) and the suction coming from the evaporator to be flooding back
Unit has pulled down below zero. 
Due to the units age I will be requesting the replacement of the TXV and Condenser Skid to prevent any further issues.
Due to the heavy flow of traffic in the kitchen a second tech is needed for safety.
The existing condensing unit is obsolete. The replacement condensing unit is physically bigger and requires a 20 amp circuit not a 15 amp circuit.
Recovered gas from system. Cut out old skid, skid very heavy had tech onsite assist with Removal and setting new skid.
Removed txv and flushed coil with nitrogen. Found new valve had to be refitted and piped due to not being oem parts (this took a while with it not being oem ).
Used 3/8 street 90 from truck stock.  ....  Used 1/2 copper pipe from truck stock
After all connections pressure tested system and held for 10-15 min. Pulled deep vacuum below 500 microns. While in vacuum wired in electrical. Broke vacuum with charge, added 3 lbs R404A.

I then went to controllers and found mercury controllers programmed to not have a defrost. This store does not have rdm so these controllers are stand alone. I then programmed controls to have defrost wvery 6 hours for a min of 30 mins. I then tested defrost and found low pressure control not cutting off compressor at desired pressure and compressor going into vacuum. I then isolated and replaced dual pressure control and set pressure cut offs accordingly. I then went down and verified program on evaps and found superheat set to 4 degrees on all 3 evaps. Need to order copeland scroll coresense controller, emerson oil management control, and 4-20 trans ma 0-200 transducer. Summary unit number one comp 3 loop needs a leak search and repair of the leak, replace the low and high pressure switches charge the unit with fresh R290, board, and Dexell controller, and needs new communication wire with female and male plugs. Then after the Dexell controller reads the other 2 units we can inspect the operation of units 2 and 3. Found the Main controller in both 104 and 105 are bad.

After completely the txv cleaning, I vacuumed the circuit down to 300 microns. Released refrigerant and performed a leak search. There were no leaks on this circuit but when walking by another circuit the leak detector went off, 4-34 had a leak on the sorton valve, verified with electronic leak detector and bubbles, tightened the component that was leaking. Verified that there were no more leaks in circuit 34 with leak detector and bubbles. A seafood case also went off on the leak detector, will be returning tonight at 8:30 to repair leak in seafood case. Returned to store and checked in with bakery manager. The bottom section of the seafood case was already pulled. Removed deck pans and performed leak search. Was not picking up any leaks on the bottom section. Once the ice and trays were removed from the top section located the leak on the distributor where the expansion valve was brazed onto. Verified the location of the leak with leak detector and bubbles. Pumped down the circuit then removed powerhead and expansion valve internals so they would not overheat. Used a torch and went around the braze joint to run the existing excess solder around the joint. Once the braze joint was cleaned up checked it with a mirror. Pulled vacuum on the circuit and made sure the vacuum held. Put the circuit back into refrigeration then performed additional electronic leak search. There were no other leaks found. B6642513-9297-4B47-B675-F1C5C162F53E.root_cause: Found that the high pressure was due to noncondensables in the system. Likey yesterday, the system tripped on high head and was tripped until ambient temps droped. The noncondensables was due to the Pressureswitch being set into a vaccuum, and leaks on suction side shrader, flare off of pressure switch, and rotolock fitting. Roto lock fitting likely has a crushed gasket, so we should return to replace it, as for now its sealed but likely will leak again. I then unthreaded the roto lock and pulled out the old gasket which indeed was crushed badly. I then oiled up the new gasket and seated it all the way in. I then threaded the fitting back on being sure it wasn’t cross threaded and fully tight on there. After that I then got ready to pull a vacuum. I pulled it to 500 microns and let it sit on the vacuum for extended period of time as it had an active leak for quite some time and was having some pressure spikes. Wanted to be sure I got all non condensables out. I then saw that the heater safety switch wires were burned together and one of them was completely burned off of its connector just hanging in the cabinet. I then took out the old heater safety switch and took it to RSD to get a new one. I got the new one and checked it with meter to insure it was hood and it was so I installed it. Wired it back onto H2 and H3.

D1F710A8-1B68-4296-873D-4B4F60238027.root_cause: I observed there to be no floating ball on the rack oil reservoir. I found the oil control to be struggling to fill. I found compressor 5 and 8 both off at the breaker. I checked and found both compressors to not be valved off. I valved off both compressors 5 and 8. I found both compressors 5 and 8 had full sight glass of oil on the oil control. Both compressors are written up in separate WOs. We will need to quote to replace the oil control on compressor 4 and add oil to the rack to obtain a floating ball in the rack oil reservoir. The rack is maintaining proper operating pressures at this time. No other issues found. This call needs a quote. I observed there to be compressor lockout alarms. I checked and found the rack oil level to be low. I located two gallons of POE oil from truck stock. I added the two gallons to the rack. This brought the oil level for each compressor up. I monitored the racks operations. I verified there to be no active alarms. The rack is operating properly at this time. When the parts for quoted work arrives we will return to finish repairs. This call needs a quote.

0FCDE23A-C5DC-405B-AAA7-F1A4B5D5C6C8.root_cause: Found that old sensor was damaged.

69A302A7-6DE3-4558-9A36-C89CF03E2445.root_cause: Found that sensor 4 is in T2 case left side 7F degrees warmer that actual. Replaced the sensor and checked. Case temp now correct. Found a faulty discharge sensor on T2. I replaced the sensor and now is working properly on temperature.

4FA6BD75-5269-49A7-86E8-6C10FA0F5204.root_cause: Found temp sensor broken. Found compressor 3 found 1 blown fuse. That’s why fans would not run. Because my suction temp sensor is on number 3 and it was reading warm. That’s why fans wouldn’t work.

3D6B3A3E-EB29-4BB6-A550-D60525562187.root_cause: Found leak at receiver service valve. Found service cap loose.

5C1CA077-0B4D-4BB7-A24D-780627B0F88A.root_cause: Previously bursted compressor discharge check valve. Cut out defective ball valve. 04253C6B-E8BA-4614-B526-90A16B6F48F4.root_cause: Found the motor with the broken blade.

D2BB3C7C-5214-48F9-9547-05DB427108B6.root_cause: Found that TXV icing over during operation. Found that TXV was bad. TXV was the wrong one for the olive bar. New TXV is rated for R290 where the case is a R449a case. Was able to change out the old TXV body with the new one that was delivered. System was still behaving as if there was a restriction at the TXV. Had only 12 psi at the outlet of Evap coil and TXV and liquid line immediately began freezing. CaseArts made the mistake of determining that the correct orifice size for that specific case was a 0 and I was told that the size 2 that was sent with the wrong TXV body was the correct size for the correct TXV body that was sent and delivered. Installed the H02 orifice, pulled vacuum, critically charged unit to listed amount of R449a once again, and restarted unit. There is no more blockage at the TXV after restart and pressure is normal on outlet of Evap. Set SH to read 7-10. Case came down and was properly cycling at the previous setpoint of +36. No issues of short cycling or frost build up on dist tubes of TXV itself. Sight glass shows full column of liquid during operation.

4F986BDD-0FAB-4020-9FE7-5DB6F66F75D5.root_cause: Found case drain back up with water due to clogged drain. Blew drain out with co2 which cleared clog and changed a bad fan motor.

D8A619CA-7FE3-47FF-82CD-20F79DBAD60B.root_cause: Had 1 motor out on the produce prep cooler. Sourced motor from the truck and replaced defective motor.

91CB6688-01C6-4EEA-9432-834E32DED581.root_cause: Found condenser split valve is leaking by.

B58CD653-7A50-454A-9FB1-DEAB2B898D7E.root_cause: Pulled case and found fan motor was bad. Installed new motor.

If problem happens again recommends replacing fan due to plug not holding tightly. High pressure cutout had been tripped. Reset the HPS and the unit kicked on and started cooling the box down from 12°. Checked the discharge pressure graph and found discharge pressure got up to 260psi, the high pressure cutout is 395psi. The DTC valve that regulates the scroll head temp was not feeding, this would cause the compressor to run hotter than normal, usually causing the overload to open until it cooled down enough, OR a high pressure event that tripped the HPS. Unplugged the EEV that controls the flow of cooled gas to cool down scroll discharge, and spun it Half a turn and this opened up the valve to allow cooling. Fixed the valve open 1/4 of a turn to ensure the unit will stay running until I can further trouble shoot which component on the CoreSense is faulty, the thermistor, the EEV or the controls. Found the low pressure control was stuck open, it’s set to close at 20ish PSI and suction was around 50psi. Forced the LP controller closed to bring box temp down and monitored the pressures and discharge temps while prepping a new LP controller for install. Turned power off to unit and installed the new control.

Fans 3 & 4 came back online and head pressure dropped down to 264 psi. All three legs on CFM 4 are drawing 2.5-2.7 amps. Monitored head pressure and it has been maintaining 260-270 psi. Alarms cleared. Rack has been maintaining 20-30% receiver level since leak repair.

37F780D7-C742-4672-9ED5-CB4A4B1BDFAE.root_cause: I found the flare fitting going into the top of the oil filter were leaking. I was able to get a full turn to tighten them down and stop the seeping of oil. The oil reservoir has no ball floating in it. I suspect that the compressors go to fill there float up after using some of the oil and circulating it and there’s not enough to get the pressure up and it locks out on low oil pressure. I also found comp 3 and comp 6 are both isolated due to pending repairs by insource. These compressor are full of oil and no longer circulating with the rest of the compressors inturn holding that oil back. Site glass for the oil filter was empty so after I tightend connections I cleaned up oil from around the filter and added two gallons of Poe. Site glass filled and seperator began to fill and is starting to show oil at the first glass it will continue to fill as oil gets circulated back thru and into the seperator. With system being two compressor down this changes the velocity at which the oil is able to be brought back. There may also be oil getting trapped in the lines as there’s not enough volocity to properly get it all back.

Cleaned areas to be resealed. Resealed left, right sides, entire back of case.

8D0F85D5-6DAE-4209-AC76-55F06B493CA9.root_cause: Checked oil and found the compressors cycling on and off with oil failure

Isolated and pumped down that section of the piping and put a stick of braze on the whole T fitting to strengthen it and seal it up. After repair I used nitrogen and trace gas to pressure test the isolated section and it passed a standing pressure test. I also used my leak detector and bubbles to verify it was good.
